-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).


## VIII.26.14 Aggregation (`AGG`)

-   **Crate:** `crates/strata-exec/agg`.
-   **Measurement focus:** CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Micro entry point:** `cargo bench -p strata-exec --bench perf -- agg`.
-   **End-to-end entry point:** `strata-bench run scenarios/agg/`.

### PT-AGG-BASELINE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** HW-REF-1, SF=1 dataset relevant to the subsystem, default settings, warm caches unless the subsystem is I/O.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Correct baseline throughput on HW-REF-1 at SF=1; establishes ledger value.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-AGG-SCALING-CORES
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** cpuset restricted per step (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers); same dataset; SMT disabled for the sweep.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Throughput at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers; efficiency ≥ 80% up to 16 workers for parallelizable work.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-AGG-SCALING-DATA
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** SF 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 with identical schema and distributions.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Behavior at SF 0.01 → 10; cost per row must stay within 1.3× across scale.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-AGG-SKEW
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** datasets regenerated with Zipf exponent 0, 1.1, 2.0 on the dominant key.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Zipf s ∈ {0, 1.1, 2.0} on the dominant key; no worker > 2× median busy time.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-AGG-MEMORY-LIMIT
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** max_memory_usage set to 25% of the peak observed in the baseline run; spill enabled.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Run with memory limit at 25% of unconstrained peak; must spill or fail cleanly, never OOM.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-AGG-CANCELLATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** 1,000 runs each cancelled at a uniformly random time between 0 and the baseline duration.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Cancel at random points; all resources released within 10 ms p99; no leaked reservations.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-AGG-CONCURRENCY
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** 64 concurrent clients, open-loop arrival at 80% of measured saturation.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** 64 concurrent instances; aggregate throughput ≥ 0.8× single-instance × min(64, cores).
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-AGG-COLD-VS-WARM
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** run after `drop_caches` and engine cache clear, then immediately again.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Report both; cold must reach ≥ 85% of device bandwidth where I/O-bound.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-AGG-ISA-TIERS
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** `STRATA_FORCE_ISA` set to scalar, x86-64-v3, x86-64-v4 on x86 runners and neon / sve on ARM runners.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Run with dispatch forced to scalar, v3, v4, NEON; results identical; speedups recorded.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** every PR (SF=0.1).

### PT-AGG-ALLOCATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** counting global allocator build (`--features alloc-count`), 10,000 batches after 100-batch warmup.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Counting allocator: steady-state allocations per batch equals documented value (usually 0).
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** every PR (SF=0.1).

### PT-AGG-LONG-RUN
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** 6-hour soak with mixed load representative of the subsystem.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** 6-hour soak; no throughput decay > 10%, no RSS growth > 5% after warmup.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-AGG-REGRESSION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** same scenario as baseline on the dedicated runner; compared to rolling 10-run window.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Compared against rolling baseline (STRATA-SYS-19-005); blocks merge on significant regression.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** every PR (SF=0.1).

### PT-AGG-NOISY-NEIGHBOR
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** `stress-ng --cpu N --io 4 --vm 2` in a sibling cgroup with equal weight.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Run alongside a CPU+IO hog in another cgroup; degradation documented and bounded by quotas.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-AGG-FAILURE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** fault from VIII.24 injected for 30 s then cleared.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Inject relevant I/O faults from VIII.24; performance recovers to baseline within 60 s after fault clears.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-AGG-OBSERVABILITY
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Aggregation.
-   **Setup:** baseline scenario with metrics scrape every 1 s and EXPLAIN ANALYZE enabled.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `agg` scenario set under this setup; CPR by group cardinality 1e1–1e9; two-level switch point; partial-agg abandonment.
-   **Pass criterion:** Every metric/EXPLAIN counter for the subsystem is populated and plausible (cross-checked against PMU or OS counters).
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

-   **Procedure:** execute the `sort` scenario set under this setup; rows/s for sort widths 4–64 bytes; top-K by k; external sort passes.
-   **Pass criterion:** Run with dispatch forced to scalar, v3, v4, NEON; results identical; speedups recorded.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** every PR (SF=0.1).

### PT-SORT-ALLOCATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Sort and top-K.
-   **Setup:** counting global allocator build (`--features alloc-count`), 10,000 batches after 100-batch warmup.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `sort` scenario set under this setup; rows/s for sort widths 4–64 bytes; top-K by k; external sort passes.
-   **Pass criterion:** Counting allocator: steady-state allocations per batch equals documented value (usually 0).
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** every PR (SF=0.1).

### PT-SORT-LONG-RUN
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Sort and top-K.
-   **Setup:** 6-hour soak with mixed load representative of the subsystem.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `sort` scenario set under this setup; rows/s for sort widths 4–64 bytes; top-K by k; external sort passes.
-   **Pass criterion:** 6-hour soak; no throughput decay > 10%, no RSS growth > 5% after warmup.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-SORT-REGRESSION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Sort and top-K.
-   **Setup:** same scenario as baseline on the dedicated runner; compared to rolling 10-run window.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `sort` scenario set under this setup; rows/s for sort widths 4–64 bytes; top-K by k; external sort passes.
-   **Pass criterion:** Compared against rolling baseline (STRATA-SYS-19-005); blocks merge on significant regression.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** every PR (SF=0.1).

### PT-SORT-NOISY-NEIGHBOR
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Sort and top-K.
-   **Setup:** `stress-ng --cpu N --io 4 --vm 2` in a sibling cgroup with equal weight.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `sort` scenario set under this setup; rows/s for sort widths 4–64 bytes; top-K by k; external sort passes.
-   **Pass criterion:** Run alongside a CPU+IO hog in another cgroup; degradation documented and bounded by quotas.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-SORT-FAILURE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Sort and top-K.
-   **Setup:** fault from VIII.24 injected for 30 s then cleared.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `sort` scenario set under this setup; rows/s for sort widths 4–64 bytes; top-K by k; external sort passes.
-   **Pass criterion:** Inject relevant I/O faults from VIII.24; performance recovers to baseline within 60 s after fault clears.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-SORT-OBSERVABILITY
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Sort and top-K.
-   **Setup:** baseline scenario with metrics scrape every 1 s and EXPLAIN ANALYZE enabled.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `sort` scenario set under this setup; rows/s for sort widths 4–64 bytes; top-K by k; external sort passes.
-   **Pass criterion:** Every metric/EXPLAIN counter for the subsystem is populated and plausible (cross-checked against PMU or OS counters).
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).


## VIII.26.17 Spill (`SPILL`)

-   **Crate:** `crates/strata-exec/spill`.
-   **Measurement focus:** spill write/read GB/s; slowdown factor vs in-memory (target ≤ 3× at 2× memory oversubscription).
-   **Micro entry point:** `cargo bench -p strata-exec --bench perf -- spill`.
-   **End-to-end entry point:** `strata-bench run scenarios/spill/`.

### PT-SPILL-BASELINE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Spill.
-   **Setup:** HW-REF-1, SF=1 dataset relevant to the subsystem, default settings, warm caches unless the subsystem is I/O.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `spill` scenario set under this setup; spill write/read GB/s; slowdown factor vs in-memory (target ≤ 3× at 2× memory oversubscription).
-   **Pass criterion:** Correct baseline throughput on HW-REF-1 at SF=1; establishes ledger value.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-SPILL-SCALING-CORES
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Spill.
-   **Setup:** cpuset restricted per step (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers); same dataset; SMT disabled for the sweep.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `spill` scenario set under this setup; spill write/read GB/s; slowdown factor vs in-memory (target ≤ 3× at 2× memory oversubscription).
-   **Pass criterion:** Throughput at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers; efficiency ≥ 80% up to 16 workers for parallelizable work.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-SPILL-SCALING-DATA
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Spill.
-   **Setup:** SF 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 with identical schema and distributions.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `spill` scenario set under this setup; spill write/read GB/s; slowdown factor vs in-memory (target ≤ 3× at 2× memory oversubscription).
-   **Pass criterion:** Behavior at SF 0.01 → 10; cost per row must stay within 1.3× across scale.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-SPILL-SKEW
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Spill.
-   **Setup:** datasets regenerated with Zipf exponent 0, 1.1, 2.0 on the dominant key.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `spill` scenario set under this setup; spill write/read GB/s; slowdown factor vs in-memory (target ≤ 3× at 2× memory oversubscription).
-   **Pass criterion:** Zipf s ∈ {0, 1.1, 2.0} on the dominant key; no worker > 2× median busy time.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-SPILL-MEMORY-LIMIT
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Spill.
-   **Setup:** max_memory_usage set to 25% of the peak observed in the baseline run; spill enabled.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `spill` scenario set under this setup; spill write/read GB/s; slowdown factor vs in-memory (target ≤ 3× at 2× memory oversubscription).
-   **Pass criterion:** Run with memory limit at 25% of unconstrained peak; must spill or fail cleanly, never OOM.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-SPILL-CANCELLATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Spill.
-   **Setup:** 1,000 runs each cancelled at a uniformly random time between 0 and the baseline duration.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `spill` scenario set under this setup; spill write/read GB/s; slowdown factor vs in-memory (target ≤ 3× at 2× memory oversubscription).
-   **Pass criterion:** Cancel at random points; all resources released within 10 ms p99; no leaked reservations.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-SPILL-CONCURRENCY
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Spill.
-   **Setup:** 64 concurrent clients, open-loop arrival at 80% of measured saturation.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `spill` scenario set under this setup; spill write/read GB/s; slowdown factor vs in-memory (target ≤ 3× at 2× memory oversubscription).
-   **Pass criterion:** 64 concurrent instances; aggregate throughput ≥ 0.8× single-instance × min(64, cores).
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

-   **Setup:** SF 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 with identical schema and distributions.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** Behavior at SF 0.01 → 10; cost per row must stay within 1.3× across scale.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-CACHE-SKEW
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Caches.
-   **Setup:** datasets regenerated with Zipf exponent 0, 1.1, 2.0 on the dominant key.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** Zipf s ∈ {0, 1.1, 2.0} on the dominant key; no worker > 2× median busy time.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-CACHE-MEMORY-LIMIT
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Caches.
-   **Setup:** max_memory_usage set to 25% of the peak observed in the baseline run; spill enabled.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** Run with memory limit at 25% of unconstrained peak; must spill or fail cleanly, never OOM.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-CACHE-CANCELLATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Caches.
-   **Setup:** 1,000 runs each cancelled at a uniformly random time between 0 and the baseline duration.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** Cancel at random points; all resources released within 10 ms p99; no leaked reservations.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-CACHE-CONCURRENCY
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Caches.
-   **Setup:** 64 concurrent clients, open-loop arrival at 80% of measured saturation.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** 64 concurrent instances; aggregate throughput ≥ 0.8× single-instance × min(64, cores).
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-CACHE-COLD-VS-WARM
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Caches.
-   **Setup:** run after `drop_caches` and engine cache clear, then immediately again.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** Report both; cold must reach ≥ 85% of device bandwidth where I/O-bound.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-CACHE-ISA-TIERS
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Caches.
-   **Setup:** `STRATA_FORCE_ISA` set to scalar, x86-64-v3, x86-64-v4 on x86 runners and neon / sve on ARM runners.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** Run with dispatch forced to scalar, v3, v4, NEON; results identical; speedups recorded.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** every PR (SF=0.1).

### PT-CACHE-ALLOCATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Caches.
-   **Setup:** counting global allocator build (`--features alloc-count`), 10,000 batches after 100-batch warmup.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** Counting allocator: steady-state allocations per batch equals documented value (usually 0).
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** every PR (SF=0.1).

### PT-CACHE-LONG-RUN
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Caches.
-   **Setup:** 6-hour soak with mixed load representative of the subsystem.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** 6-hour soak; no throughput decay > 10%, no RSS growth > 5% after warmup.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-CACHE-REGRESSION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Caches.
-   **Setup:** same scenario as baseline on the dedicated runner; compared to rolling 10-run window.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** Compared against rolling baseline (STRATA-SYS-19-005); blocks merge on significant regression.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** every PR (SF=0.1).

### PT-CACHE-NOISY-NEIGHBOR
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Caches.
-   **Setup:** `stress-ng --cpu N --io 4 --vm 2` in a sibling cgroup with equal weight.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** Run alongside a CPU+IO hog in another cgroup; degradation documented and bounded by quotas.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-CACHE-FAILURE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Caches.
-   **Setup:** fault from VIII.24 injected for 30 s then cleared.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** Inject relevant I/O faults from VIII.24; performance recovers to baseline within 60 s after fault clears.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-CACHE-OBSERVABILITY
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Caches.
-   **Setup:** baseline scenario with metrics scrape every 1 s and EXPLAIN ANALYZE enabled.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `cache` scenario set under this setup; hit latency, hit ratio under Zipf access, scan resistance effectiveness.
-   **Pass criterion:** Every metric/EXPLAIN counter for the subsystem is populated and plausible (cross-checked against PMU or OS counters).
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Full-text and string search.

-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-TXT-SCALING-CORES
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Full-text and string search.
-   **Setup:** cpuset restricted per step (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers); same dataset; SMT disabled for the sweep.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `txt` scenario set under this setup; GB/s substring; token index lookup latency; regex literal prefilter benefit.
-   **Pass criterion:** Throughput at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers; efficiency ≥ 80% up to 16 workers for parallelizable work.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-TXT-SCALING-DATA
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Full-text and string search.
-   **Setup:** SF 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 with identical schema and distributions.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `txt` scenario set under this setup; GB/s substring; token index lookup latency; regex literal prefilter benefit.
-   **Pass criterion:** Behavior at SF 0.01 → 10; cost per row must stay within 1.3× across scale.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-TXT-SKEW
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Full-text and string search.
-   **Setup:** datasets regenerated with Zipf exponent 0, 1.1, 2.0 on the dominant key.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `txt` scenario set under this setup; GB/s substring; token index lookup latency; regex literal prefilter benefit.
-   **Pass criterion:** Zipf s ∈ {0, 1.1, 2.0} on the dominant key; no worker > 2× median busy time.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-TXT-MEMORY-LIMIT
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Full-text and string search.
-   **Setup:** max_memory_usage set to 25% of the peak observed in the baseline run; spill enabled.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `txt` scenario set under this setup; GB/s substring; token index lookup latency; regex literal prefilter benefit.
-   **Pass criterion:** Run with memory limit at 25% of unconstrained peak; must spill or fail cleanly, never OOM.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-TXT-CANCELLATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Full-text and string search.
-   **Setup:** 1,000 runs each cancelled at a uniformly random time between 0 and the baseline duration.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `txt` scenario set under this setup; GB/s substring; token index lookup latency; regex literal prefilter benefit.
-   **Pass criterion:** Cancel at random points; all resources released within 10 ms p99; no leaked reservations.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-TXT-CONCURRENCY
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Full-text and string search.
-   **Setup:** 64 concurrent clients, open-loop arrival at 80% of measured saturation.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `txt` scenario set under this setup; GB/s substring; token index lookup latency; regex literal prefilter benefit.
-   **Pass criterion:** 64 concurrent instances; aggregate throughput ≥ 0.8× single-instance × min(64, cores).
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-TXT-COLD-VS-WARM
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Full-text and string search.
-   **Setup:** run after `drop_caches` and engine cache clear, then immediately again.

-   **Pass criterion:** Report both; cold must reach ≥ 85% of device bandwidth where I/O-bound.

-   **Pass criterion:** Report both; cold must reach ≥ 85% of device bandwidth where I/O-bound.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-REC-ISA-TIERS
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Startup and recovery.
-   **Setup:** `STRATA_FORCE_ISA` set to scalar, x86-64-v3, x86-64-v4 on x86 runners and neon / sve on ARM runners.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `rec` scenario set under this setup; startup time vs part count; WAL replay MB/s.
-   **Pass criterion:** Run with dispatch forced to scalar, v3, v4, NEON; results identical; speedups recorded.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** every PR (SF=0.1).

### PT-REC-ALLOCATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Startup and recovery.
-   **Setup:** counting global allocator build (`--features alloc-count`), 10,000 batches after 100-batch warmup.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `rec` scenario set under this setup; startup time vs part count; WAL replay MB/s.
-   **Pass criterion:** Counting allocator: steady-state allocations per batch equals documented value (usually 0).
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** every PR (SF=0.1).

### PT-REC-LONG-RUN
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Startup and recovery.
-   **Setup:** 6-hour soak with mixed load representative of the subsystem.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `rec` scenario set under this setup; startup time vs part count; WAL replay MB/s.
-   **Pass criterion:** 6-hour soak; no throughput decay > 10%, no RSS growth > 5% after warmup.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-REC-REGRESSION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Startup and recovery.
-   **Setup:** same scenario as baseline on the dedicated runner; compared to rolling 10-run window.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `rec` scenario set under this setup; startup time vs part count; WAL replay MB/s.
-   **Pass criterion:** Compared against rolling baseline (STRATA-SYS-19-005); blocks merge on significant regression.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** every PR (SF=0.1).

### PT-REC-NOISY-NEIGHBOR
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Startup and recovery.
-   **Setup:** `stress-ng --cpu N --io 4 --vm 2` in a sibling cgroup with equal weight.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `rec` scenario set under this setup; startup time vs part count; WAL replay MB/s.
-   **Pass criterion:** Run alongside a CPU+IO hog in another cgroup; degradation documented and bounded by quotas.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-REC-FAILURE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Startup and recovery.
-   **Setup:** fault from VIII.24 injected for 30 s then cleared.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `rec` scenario set under this setup; startup time vs part count; WAL replay MB/s.
-   **Pass criterion:** Inject relevant I/O faults from VIII.24; performance recovers to baseline within 60 s after fault clears.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-REC-OBSERVABILITY
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Startup and recovery.
-   **Setup:** baseline scenario with metrics scrape every 1 s and EXPLAIN ANALYZE enabled.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `rec` scenario set under this setup; startup time vs part count; WAL replay MB/s.
-   **Pass criterion:** Every metric/EXPLAIN counter for the subsystem is populated and plausible (cross-checked against PMU or OS counters).
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).


## VIII.26.25 Security fast paths (`SEC`)

-   **Crate:** `crates/strata-security`.
-   **Measurement focus:** auth fast-path latency; RLS predicate overhead; encryption at rest overhead (target ≤ 5%).
-   **Micro entry point:** `cargo bench -p strata-security --bench perf -- sec`.
-   **End-to-end entry point:** `strata-bench run scenarios/sec/`.

### PT-SEC-BASELINE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Security fast paths.
-   **Setup:** HW-REF-1, SF=1 dataset relevant to the subsystem, default settings, warm caches unless the subsystem is I/O.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `sec` scenario set under this setup; auth fast-path latency; RLS predicate overhead; encryption at rest overhead (target ≤ 5%).
-   **Pass criterion:** Correct baseline throughput on HW-REF-1 at SF=1; establishes ledger value.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-SEC-SCALING-CORES
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Security fast paths.
-   **Setup:** cpuset restricted per step (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers); same dataset; SMT disabled for the sweep.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `sec` scenario set under this setup; auth fast-path latency; RLS predicate overhead; encryption at rest overhead (target ≤ 5%).
-   **Pass criterion:** Throughput at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers; efficiency ≥ 80% up to 16 workers for parallelizable work.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-SEC-SCALING-DATA
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Security fast paths.
-   **Setup:** SF 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 with identical schema and distributions.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `sec` scenario set under this setup; auth fast-path latency; RLS predicate overhead; encryption at rest overhead (target ≤ 5%).
-   **Pass criterion:** Behavior at SF 0.01 → 10; cost per row must stay within 1.3× across scale.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** weekly / pre-release.

### PT-SEC-SKEW
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Security fast paths.
-   **Setup:** datasets regenerated with Zipf exponent 0, 1.1, 2.0 on the dominant key.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `sec` scenario set under this setup; auth fast-path latency; RLS predicate overhead; encryption at rest overhead (target ≤ 5%).
-   **Pass criterion:** Zipf s ∈ {0, 1.1, 2.0} on the dominant key; no worker > 2× median busy time.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-SEC-MEMORY-LIMIT
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Security fast paths.
-   **Setup:** max_memory_usage set to 25% of the peak observed in the baseline run; spill enabled.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `sec` scenario set under this setup; auth fast-path latency; RLS predicate overhead; encryption at rest overhead (target ≤ 5%).
-   **Pass criterion:** Run with memory limit at 25% of unconstrained peak; must spill or fail cleanly, never OOM.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.
-   **CI cadence:** nightly (SF=1).

### PT-SEC-CANCELLATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Subsystem:** Security fast paths.
-   **Setup:** 1,000 runs each cancelled at a uniformly random time between 0 and the baseline duration.
-   **Procedure:** execute the `sec` scenario set under this setup; auth fast-path latency; RLS predicate overhead; encryption at rest overhead (target ≤ 5%).
-   **Pass criterion:** Cancel at random points; all resources released within 10 ms p99; no leaked reservations.
-   **Artifacts:** raw samples (CSV/Parquet), run manifest (STRATA-SYS-19-004), flamegraph (SVG), PMU counter summary, `system.query_log` extract, and the comparison report against baseline.

### PT-SEC-CONCURRENCY
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Subsystem:** Security fast paths.

-   **Pass criterion:** 64 concurrent instances; aggregate throughput ≥ 0.8× single-instance × min(64, cores).

# VIII.27 Hardware reference profiles

Numeric targets in Part VIII are stated against these profiles. The benchmark laboratory MUST maintain at least HW-REF-1, HW-REF-3, HW-REF-4, and HW-REF-8 continuously; others are run before each minor release.

| Profile | Name | CPU | Memory | Storage | Network | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HW-REF-1 | Primary reference server | 1× x86-64 32C/64T (AVX-512), 3.0–3.8 GHz | 256 GiB DDR5-4800, 8 channels | 4× PCIe Gen4 enterprise NVMe with PLP, ~6.5 GB/s read each | 25 GbE | all published headline results |
| HW-REF-2 | Dual-socket NUMA server | 2× x86-64 48C/96T each | 1 TiB DDR5, 16 channels, 2 NUMA nodes | 8× PCIe Gen4 NVMe, split across sockets | 2× 100 GbE | NUMA placement validation; scaling beyond one socket |
| HW-REF-3 | ARM64 server | 1× ARM Neoverse V-class 64C (SVE2) | 256 GiB DDR5 | 4× NVMe | 25 GbE | ARM kernels, NEON/SVE dispatch, memory ordering correctness |
| HW-REF-4 | Cloud general-purpose VM | 16 vCPU (8 physical), x86-64 | 64 GiB | network block storage (provisioned 16k IOPS, 1 GB/s) + local NVMe instance store | 12.5 Gbit/s | cloud defaults, fsync on network block, noisy neighbor |
| HW-REF-5 | Small edge / developer box | 8C/16T x86-64 (AVX2 only) | 32 GiB | 1× consumer NVMe, volatile write cache | 1 GbE | low-resource defaults; consumer fsync latency |
| HW-REF-6 | Object-storage compute node | 32 vCPU | 128 GiB | local NVMe cache 2 TB + S3-compatible object store | 25 Gbit/s | tiered storage, hedging, cache admission |
| HW-REF-7 | Apple Silicon laptop (dev only) | M-series 10–16 cores | 32–64 GiB unified | internal NVMe | Wi-Fi/1 GbE | developer experience; threadpool I/O backend; NEON |
| HW-REF-8 | Container-limited pod | cgroup cpu.max = 4 CPUs on a 64-core host | memory.max = 16 GiB | shared NVMe via CSI | pod network | cgroup-aware sizing, throttling, PSI response |

## HW-REF-1 — Primary reference server

## VIII.27.9 Initial targets by profile

| Target | HW-REF-1 | HW-REF-2 | HW-REF-3 | HW-REF-4 | HW-REF-5 | HW-REF-6 | HW-REF-7 | HW-REF-8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Short query p99 at 200 clients | 25 ms | 30 ms | 35 ms | 60 ms | 80 ms | 40 ms | n/a | 120 ms |
| Single-column warm scan, rows/s/core | 1.2 B | 1.1 B | 0.9 B | 0.8 B | 0.9 B | 1.0 B | 0.7 B | 0.8 B |
| Bulk ingest sustained rows/s | 8 M | 20 M | 7 M | 1.5 M | 1 M | 4 M | 0.5 M | 0.8 M |
| Small-batch ingest ack p99 | 2 ms | 2 ms | 2.5 ms | 15 ms | 30 ms | 3 ms | n/a | 10 ms |
| Hash agg 1e8 groups, CPR | 25 | 28 | 30 | 35 | 35 | 30 | 40 | 35 |
| Join build 1e8 rows probe 1e9, s | 6 | 3.5 | 7 | 30 | 45 | 12 | n/a | 40 |
| Cold scan fraction of device bandwidth | ≥ 85% | ≥ 85% | ≥ 85% | ≥ 80% | ≥ 80% | ≥ 70% (object) | n/a | ≥ 75% |
| WAL replay MB/s | ≥ 1,000 | ≥ 1,500 | ≥ 900 | ≥ 300 | ≥ 300 | ≥ 600 | ≥ 200 | ≥ 250 |
| Startup with 1M parts, s | ≤ 2 | ≤ 2 | ≤ 2.5 | ≤ 5 | ≤ 6 | ≤ 4 (cached metadata) | ≤ 8 | ≤ 6 |
| Idle memory, 10k connections | ≤ 640 MiB | ≤ 640 MiB | ≤ 640 MiB | ≤ 640 MiB | ≤ 640 MiB | ≤ 640 MiB | ≤ 640 MiB | ≤ 640 MiB |

These are engineering targets to be re-baselined after first measurement; a missed target is a tracked gap with an owner, never a reason to weaken correctness or durability.

# VIII.28 Performance troubleshooting runbooks

Each runbook follows symptom → diagnosis → action. Every diagnosis step uses only built-in system tables and metrics, so that it works without external tooling. Runbooks are shipped in `docs/runbooks/` and linked from alerts.

## VIII.28.1 Interactive queries slow, CPU not saturated

**Diagnosis**

1.  Check `strata_query_seconds{phase="queue"}` — high queue time means admission slots are exhausted.
1.  Check `strata_sched_runqueue_seconds{class="interactive"}` — high means morsels wait behind other work.
1.  Check `strata_io_latency_seconds` p99 per device — a degraded device stalls scans.
1.  Run `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on a slow fingerprint; look for `io_wait` dominating operator time.

**Actions**

-   If queue-bound: raise `sched.interactive_slots` or reduce batch slots.
-   If I/O-bound on one device: check `strata_device_degraded`; move parts away; replace device.
-   If prefetch window small: verify `io.prefetch_window_granules` adapts (wasted ratio < 0.05).

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.2 Interactive queries slow, CPU saturated

**Diagnosis**

1.  Top fingerprints by CPU: `SELECT fingerprint, sum(cpu_us) FROM system.query_log WHERE event_time > now() - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10`.
1.  Check background share: `strata_sched_cpu_seconds_total{class="background"}` rate.
1.  Check `strata_cgroup_cpu_throttled_seconds_total` — container quota may be the limit.

**Actions**

-   Classify heavy fingerprints as `batch` via workload rules.
-   If merges dominate due to backlog, address part count (see 'Too many parts').
-   If throttled by cgroup: raise quota or reduce worker threads to match quota.

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.3 Too many parts / inserts throttled

**Diagnosis**

1.  `SELECT table, partition, count() FROM system.parts WHERE active GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 20`.
1.  Check insert batch sizes: `SELECT quantile(0.5)(rows) FROM system.insert_log WHERE ...`.
1.  Check `strata_merge_backlog_bytes` trend and `merge.max_write_bytes_per_sec`.

**Actions**

-   Increase client batch size to ≥ 100k rows or enable `insert.async_insert`.
-   Check partition key granularity — partitions that are too fine (per hour per tenant) multiply parts.
-   Temporarily raise `merge.background_max_share`.

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.4 High insert acknowledgment latency

**Diagnosis**

1.  `strata_wal_fsync_seconds` p99 — device flush latency.
1.  `strata_wal_group_records` — group size; small groups at high load mean group delay is too low.
1.  `strata_insert_stage_seconds` by stage to find the dominant stage.

**Actions**

-   Move WAL to lower-latency device (PLP NVMe).
-   Verify the device write cache mode and PLP via `strata doctor storage`.
-   If decode stage dominates, check client format (JSON vs native).

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.5 Memory limit exceeded errors

**Diagnosis**

1.  Error message names tracker path and top consumers.
1.  `SELECT query_id, memory_peak FROM system.query_log ORDER BY memory_peak DESC LIMIT 10`.
1.  Check whether spill is enabled and spill dirs have space.

**Actions**

-   Enable or enlarge spill for aggregation/join/sort.
-   Lower `query.max_threads` for the heavy query (parallel partial states multiply memory).
-   Use approximate functions (uniqHLL12, quantileTDigest) where exactness is not required.

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.6 Process RSS much larger than tracked memory

**Diagnosis**

1.  `strata_memory_untracked_bytes` trend.
1.  Allocator stats: `SELECT * FROM system.allocator_stats`.
1.  Check huge page usage and fragmentation.

**Actions**

-   Lower allocator purge delay.
-   File a bug: untracked allocations on the data path violate STRATA-SYS-05-005; attach heap profile (`SYSTEM HEAP PROFILE START`).

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.7 Cold scans far below device bandwidth

**Diagnosis**

1.  Compare against `fio` baseline on the same device.
1.  `strata_io_inflight` — low in-flight means insufficient queue depth.
1.  Check `io.backend` actually selected (`system.host_info`).

**Actions**

-   Raise `io.max_inflight_per_device` toward measured saturation depth.
-   Enable `io.direct_scan` for large scans to avoid page-cache overhead.
-   Check read_ahead_kb and scheduler settings via `strata doctor host`.

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.8 Warm scans slower than expected

**Diagnosis**

1.  EXPLAIN ANALYZE cycles/row and IPC per operator.
1.  Check selected kernel tier in `system.kernels` — scalar fallback indicates missing ISA or detection failure.
1.  Check NUMA remote access ratio.

**Actions**

-   Use the x86-64-v3 build on AVX2 hosts.
-   Pin the process within one NUMA node for single-node-sized datasets.
-   Check codec choice — ZSTD high levels decode slower; consider `compression_preset = fast`.

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.9 Query planning is slow

**Diagnosis**

1.  `plan_us` column in query log.
1.  Number of parts touched; number of joined tables.
1.  Plan cache hit ratio for the fingerprint.

**Actions**

-   Reduce part count via merges.
-   Use parameterized queries so the plan cache hits.
-   Lower `query.optimize_time_budget_ms` for interactive class.

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.10 Join spilling unexpectedly

**Diagnosis**

1.  EXPLAIN ANALYZE: estimated vs actual build rows (Q-error).
1.  Check whether statistics are stale: `system.column_statistics.last_updated`.

**Actions**

-   `ANALYZE TABLE` to refresh statistics.
-   Swap join order explicitly or let adaptive role reversal act (check it is enabled).
-   Pre-filter the build side; enable runtime filters.

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.11 Merge write amplification too high

**Diagnosis**

1.  `strata_write_amplification` per table.
1.  Distribution of merged part sizes; repeated re-merging of large parts.

**Actions**

-   Raise `merge.write_amp_budget` discipline (lower value) and `merge.max_part_bytes`.
-   Check TTL merges re-writing large parts too often (`merge.ttl_merge_min_interval_s`).

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.12 WAL in failed (read-only) state

**Diagnosis**

1.  Server log: `WAL_FSYNC_FAILED` with device and errno.
1.  Kernel log (`dmesg`) for device errors.
1.  `strata_io_errors_total`.

**Actions**

-   Do not force writes. Investigate and replace failing device.
-   Restart after device is healthy; recovery replays only CRC-valid records.
-   Verify no data loss for acknowledged writes via insert idempotency logs.

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.13 Disk filling up

**Diagnosis**

1.  `strata_disk_free_bytes`, `strata_parts_obsolete_bytes`, `strata_snapshot_pinned_bytes`.
1.  Long-running queries pinning snapshots in `system.snapshots`.

**Actions**

-   Kill or wait for long queries pinning obsolete parts.
-   Reduce `storage.old_parts_lifetime_s` temporarily.
-   Add storage or move cold partitions to object tier.

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.14 Object-storage queries slow

**Diagnosis**

1.  `strata_object_request_seconds` p99; hedge rate.
1.  Local cache hit ratio.
1.  Request size and concurrency settings.

**Actions**

-   Increase local cache size; pin metadata.
-   Increase `object.max_concurrent_requests`.
-   Check provider throttling (HTTP 503 SlowDown).

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.15 Startup takes too long

**Diagnosis**

1.  `strata_recovery_seconds` by phase.
1.  Part count; WAL unflushed bytes at crash.

**Actions**

-   Lower `memtable.max_bytes` / checkpoint interval to bound replay.
-   Ensure `recovery.lazy_open_parts = true`.
-   Reduce part count via merges before planned restarts.

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.16 Throughput drops after hours of operation

**Diagnosis**

1.  Compare first-hour vs current throughput; merge backlog; RSS growth; cache hit ratio drift.

**Actions**

-   Look for monotonic backlog (merge underprovisioned).
-   Look for memory growth (leak) — capture heap profile.
-   Check device thermal throttling and SSD write cliff (over-provisioning).

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.17 Tail latency spikes every few seconds

**Diagnosis**

1.  Correlate with `strata_flush_seconds`, merges, and `vm.dirty` writeback.
1.  Check THP setting (`always` causes compaction stalls).
1.  Check large frees (munmap TLB shootdowns) via perf `tlb:tlb_flush`.

**Actions**

-   Set THP to madvise.
-   Lower `vm.dirty_bytes`.
-   Verify large-region frees are deferred to reclaimer (STRATA-SYS-05-003).

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

## VIII.28.18 Network-bound result transfer

**Diagnosis**

1.  `strata_net_backpressure_seconds_total` growing — client is slow.
1.  Bytes/s vs NIC capacity.

**Actions**

-   Enable wire compression (LZ4).
-   Use native or Arrow Flight instead of JSON.
-   Fetch fewer columns; aggregate server-side.

**Escalation evidence to collect:** `strata doctor host --json`, `SYSTEM DUMP DIAGNOSTICS` archive (last 15 min metrics, query log extract, profile samples, settings diff), and the EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the worst fingerprint.

# VIII.30 Implementation work breakdown for Part VIII

One implementation ticket per requirement, ordered by phase. Phases: **P0** measurement system (nothing is optimized before it can be measured); **P1** host, runtime, I/O, memory, WAL foundations; **P2** kernels, hash tables, encoding, scheduling, catalog, failure behaviour; **P3** network, optimizer, sort, join, caches. Within a phase, tickets may run in parallel unless a dependency is listed.

Ticket template fields: goal, scope, acceptance, verification, evidence, dependencies, risk. A ticket is closed only when its acceptance evidence is archived and its traceability row is updated.


## VIII.30.0 Phase P0

### SYS-T0001 — implement `STRATA-SYS-01-001` (Budgets, MUST)
-   **Goal:** Each stage above MUST emit a histogram metric named `strata_insert_stage_seconds{stage="..."}` so that budget conformance is observable in production.
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-bench + crates/strata-obs`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-OBS-BASELINE` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.
-   **Verification:** unit + differential tests, the relevant VIII.24 fault cells if persistence is touched, and the VIII.26 dimension tests for the owning subsystem.
-   **Evidence:** PR includes the Part V §9 performance evidence bundle and updates the `STRATA-SYS-01-001` row in VIII.29 from `DESIGNED`.
-   **Dependencies:** none.
-   **Risk if skipped:** correctness or durability exposure — MUST not ship without it.

### SYS-T0002 — implement `STRATA-SYS-01-002` (Budgets, MUST)
-   **Goal:** The CI performance gate MUST fail if any stage's p99 exceeds 150% of its budget on HW-REF-1 for three consecutive runs.
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-bench + crates/strata-obs`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-OBS-BASELINE` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.
-   **Verification:** unit + differential tests, the relevant VIII.24 fault cells if persistence is touched, and the VIII.26 dimension tests for the owning subsystem.
-   **Evidence:** PR includes the Part V §9 performance evidence bundle and updates the `STRATA-SYS-01-002` row in VIII.29 from `DESIGNED`.
-   **Dependencies:** none.
-   **Risk if skipped:** correctness or durability exposure — MUST not ship without it.

### SYS-T0003 — implement `STRATA-SYS-01-003` (Budgets, SHOULD)
-   **Goal:** In durability mode `async` (explicitly non-durable acknowledgment), the group-commit wait is removed and the total p50 target becomes ≤ 140 µs. The two modes MUST NOT be reported as one number.
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-bench + crates/strata-obs`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-OBS-BASELINE` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.
-   **Verification:** unit + differential tests, the relevant VIII.24 fault cells if persistence is touched, and the VIII.26 dimension tests for the owning subsystem.
-   **Evidence:** PR includes the Part V §9 performance evidence bundle and updates the `STRATA-SYS-01-003` row in VIII.29 from `DESIGNED`.
-   **Dependencies:** none.
-   **Risk if skipped:** performance opportunity left on the table; acceptable for first release with a tracked gap.

### SYS-T0004 — implement `STRATA-SYS-01-004` (Budgets, MUST)
-   **Goal:** A bulk ingest benchmark run is invalid unless it lasts long enough for at least 3 full compaction cycles at the largest level reached; short runs that end before compaction debt materializes MUST NOT be published.
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-bench + crates/strata-obs`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-OBS-BASELINE` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.

-   **Evidence:** PR includes the Part V §9 performance evidence bundle and updates the `STRATA-SYS-01-004` row in VIII.29 from `DESIGNED`.
-   **Dependencies:** none.
-   **Risk if skipped:** correctness or durability exposure — MUST not ship without it.

### SYS-T0005 — implement `STRATA-SYS-01-005` (Budgets, MUST)
-   **Goal:** The benchmark MUST report the ratio *sustained throughput / first-five-minutes throughput*; a ratio below 0.8 indicates hidden debt and blocks publication.
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-bench + crates/strata-obs`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-OBS-BASELINE` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.

-   **Goal:** For queries whose estimated work is below 2 ms of CPU, the scheduler MUST NOT fan out to more than 4 worker threads; spawning 64 tasks for a 1 ms query increases tail latency and harms concurrency.

-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-OBS-BASELINE` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.

### SYS-T0127 — implement `STRATA-SYS-04-025` (I/O engine, MUST)
-   **Goal:** On `EIO` during read, the engine MUST retry once, then mark the granule as unreadable, fail the query with `STORAGE_READ_ERROR` naming the part and column, and schedule scrub (Part IV §93) of that part. It MUST NOT return partial results silently.

### SYS-T0128 — implement `STRATA-SYS-04-026` (I/O engine, MUST)
-   **Goal:** On `EIO` from `fsync`, the engine MUST assume the written data may be lost (post-2018 Linux fsync semantics: the error is reported once and dirty pages may be dropped). For the WAL this is fatal for the affected segment: the engine MUST stop acknowledging writes, fail in-flight commits, and enter read-only mode until restart. It MUST NOT retry fsync and treat success as durability.
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-io`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-IO-BASELINE` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.

-   **Risk if skipped:** correctness or durability exposure — MUST not ship without it.

### SYS-T0158 — implement `STRATA-SYS-07-004` (WAL, MUST)
-   **Goal:** Group delay MUST be adaptive: when the previous fsync latency was L and arrival rate is low, delay = 0 (flush immediately); when the device is busy, delay grows up to `min(L, group_delay_max)`. This prevents adding latency at low load while amortizing at high load.
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-wal`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-WAL-BASELINE` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.

-   **Goal:** Degree of parallelism (DOP) per query: `dop = clamp(ceil(est_cpu_ms / target_ms_per_worker), 1, max_threads_for_class)`, where `target_ms_per_worker` = 5 ms for interactive and 50 ms for batch. DOP MUST be reduced under contention to keep total active morsels ≤ 2 × workers.

-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-ADM-BASELINE` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.
-   **Verification:** unit + differential tests, the relevant VIII.24 fault cells if persistence is touched, and the VIII.26 dimension tests for the owning subsystem.
-   **Evidence:** PR includes the Part V §9 performance evidence bundle and updates the `STRATA-SYS-11-008` row in VIII.29 from `DESIGNED`.
-   **Dependencies:** P1 runtime, I/O and memory accounting.
-   **Risk if skipped:** correctness or durability exposure — MUST not ship without it.

### SYS-T0236 — implement `STRATA-SYS-17-001` (Catalog, MUST)
-   **Goal:** The catalog state visible to queries is an immutable snapshot object (`Arc<CatalogSnapshot>`), published by atomic pointer swap (`arc-swap` or epoch-based RCU). Readers load the pointer once per query (~5 ns) and never lock.

### SYS-T0242 — implement `STRATA-SYS-06-001` (Network, MUST)
-   **Goal:** The native protocol MUST transmit data as columnar blocks in the engine's in-memory format (or Arrow IPC), so that the server performs no row-by-row transcoding on SELECT results and INSERT payloads.

### SYS-T0243 — implement `STRATA-SYS-06-002` (Network, MUST)
-   **Goal:** Every protocol MUST support streaming in both directions with bounded buffers: the server begins sending result blocks as soon as the first is ready, and pauses execution (backpressure) when the socket send buffer and the per-query output queue (`max_result_queue_blocks`, default 16) are full.
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-server/net`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-NET-BASELINE` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.

-   **Risk if skipped:** correctness or durability exposure — MUST not ship without it.

-   **Goal:** JSON output is the slowest path; its serializer MUST be vectorized per column (write all values of a column into a scratch buffer, then interleave), MUST use a fast float formatter (Ryu or equivalent shortest round-trip), and MUST be benchmarked at ≥ 400 MB/s per core output on the standard events table.

### SYS-T0262 — implement `STRATA-SYS-12-001` (Optimizer, MUST)
-   **Goal:** Join order: for ≤ 10 relations use dynamic programming over connected subgraphs (DPccp); above 10 use a greedy heuristic (GOO) followed by local improvement. Optimization time budget 5 ms for interactive class; exceeding budget returns best plan so far.
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-planner`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-OPT-BASELINE` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.

### SYS-T0263 — implement `STRATA-SYS-12-002` (Optimizer, MUST)
-   **Goal:** Build side selection: the smaller *estimated bytes* side builds, unless the larger side is already partitioned/sorted compatibly; at runtime, if the build side is observed > 4× its estimate and the probe side is smaller, the join MUST be able to swap roles before probing begins (adaptive role reversal).
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-planner`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).

### SYS-T0267 — implement `STRATA-SYS-14-001` (Sort, MUST)
-   **Goal:** Full sort uses a two-phase design: per-morsel in-memory sort of normalized keys, then a k-way merge using a loser tree. Normalized keys: all sort columns encoded into a fixed-width, memcmp-comparable byte prefix (integers big-endian with sign flip, floats with IEEE total-order transform, strings truncated prefix + tie-break pointer, NULLS FIRST/LAST as a leading byte, DESC by bitwise NOT).
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-exec/sort`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-SORT-BASELINE` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.

-   **Evidence:** PR includes the Part V §9 performance evidence bundle and updates the `STRATA-SYS-14-001` row in VIII.29 from `DESIGNED`.
-   **Dependencies:** P2 kernels and hash tables; statistics pipeline.
-   **Risk if skipped:** correctness or durability exposure — MUST not ship without it.

## VIII.30.4 Phase P4

### SYS-T0282 — implement `STRATA-SYS-37-001` (Distributed, MUST)
-   **Goal:** A distributed query over N nodes MUST achieve ≥ 0.8 × N × single-node throughput on scan-aggregate queries whose shuffle volume is < 1% of scanned bytes (scaling efficiency ≥ 80% up to 16 nodes).
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-dist`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-NET-SCALING-CORES` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.

-   **Goal:** Two-phase aggregation: each node aggregates locally and ships partial states; the coordinator (or a hash-partitioned set of reducers for high cardinality) merges. Shipping raw rows for aggregation is forbidden unless the planner proves partial aggregation gives < 1.2× reduction.
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-dist`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-NET-SCALING-CORES` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.

### SYS-T0288 — implement `STRATA-SYS-37-007` (Distributed, MUST)
-   **Goal:** Metadata consensus (Raft) MUST be off the data path: inserts commit locally to the shard leader's WAL; consensus is used for membership, schema, and part-set metadata, with batching of part-publish entries (≥ 100 per Raft entry under load).
-   **Scope:** `crates/strata-dist`; changes outside this module require an RFC (Appendix B).
-   **Acceptance:** the behaviour above is implemented behind a documented setting or as a default; `PT-NET-SCALING-CORES` (or a narrower test named in the PR) passes on HW-REF-1 and HW-REF-3; no regression > 3% on the P0 benchmark suite.
-   **Verification:** unit + differential tests, the relevant VIII.24 fault cells if persistence is touched, and the VIII.26 dimension tests for the owning subsystem.
-   **Evidence:** PR includes the Part V §9 performance evidence bundle and updates the `STRATA-SYS-37-007` row in VIII.29 from `DESIGNED`.
-   **Dependencies:** L3 release gate achieved (VIII.38).
-   **Risk if skipped:** correctness or durability exposure — MUST not ship without it.

# VIII.31 Codec catalog and selection matrix

This catalog specifies each codec's applicability, physical layout, and decode strategy, followed by the expected best codec per (type, data distribution). The selection matrix is the *expected* outcome of the sampling-based selector (STRATA-SYS-10-001) and is used as a test oracle: on the synthetic distribution datasets, the selector MUST choose the listed codec (or one within 5% size and 10% decode cost of it).

## VIII.31.1 `BitPack`

-   **Best for:** integers with bounded range after transform.
-   **Layout:** header: u8 width; payload: ceil(n×w/8) bytes, 64-value miniblocks.
-   **Decode strategy:** SIMD unpack via shuffle+shift per width (generated kernels for w=1..64).
-   **Applicable families:** int,uint,temporal,decimal,dict.
-   **Format test:** golden files `tests/format/codec/bitpack/v1/*.bin` decoded by every release (backward compatibility, Part IV §54).
-   **Fuzzing:** `cargo fuzz run codec_bitpack_decode` — decoder MUST reject malformed input with an error, never panic or read out of bounds; corpus kept in repo.

| Type | Applicable | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Int32` | yes | — |
| `Int64` | yes | — |
| `UInt32` | yes | — |
| `UInt64` | yes | — |
| `Float32` | no | not applicable |
| `Float64` | no | not applicable |
| `Decimal64` | yes | via integer representation |
| `Date32` | yes | via integer representation |
| `DateTime64` | yes | via integer representation |
| `Bool` | no | not applicable |
| `String` | no | not applicable |
| `UUID` | no | not applicable |
| `LowCardinality(String)` | yes | on dictionary codes |

## VIII.31.2 `FOR`

-   **Best for:** integers clustered around a base.
-   **Layout:** header: base (native width) + BitPack(width of max−base).
-   **Decode strategy:** add base after unpack (fused).
-   **Applicable families:** int,uint,temporal,decimal.
-   **Format test:** golden files `tests/format/codec/for/v1/*.bin` decoded by every release (backward compatibility, Part IV §54).
-   **Fuzzing:** `cargo fuzz run codec_for_decode` — decoder MUST reject malformed input with an error, never panic or read out of bounds; corpus kept in repo.

| Type | Applicable | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Int32` | yes | — |
| `Int64` | yes | — |
| `UInt32` | yes | — |
| `UInt64` | yes | — |
| `Float32` | no | not applicable |
| `Float64` | no | not applicable |
| `Decimal64` | yes | via integer representation |
| `Date32` | yes | via integer representation |
| `DateTime64` | yes | via integer representation |
| `Bool` | no | not applicable |
| `String` | no | not applicable |
| `UUID` | no | not applicable |
| `LowCardinality(String)` | no | not applicable |

## VIII.31.3 `Delta`

-   **Best for:** monotonic or slowly changing integers (ids, timestamps).
-   **Layout:** first value + zigzag deltas → BitPack per 128-value block with block min.
-   **Decode strategy:** SIMD prefix sum (4-lane/8-lane scan) fused with unpack.
-   **Applicable families:** int,uint,temporal.
-   **Format test:** golden files `tests/format/codec/delta/v1/*.bin` decoded by every release (backward compatibility, Part IV §54).
-   **Fuzzing:** `cargo fuzz run codec_delta_decode` — decoder MUST reject malformed input with an error, never panic or read out of bounds; corpus kept in repo.

| Type | Applicable | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Int32` | yes | — |
| `Int64` | yes | — |
| `UInt32` | yes | — |
| `UInt64` | yes | — |
| `Float32` | no | not applicable |
| `Float64` | no | not applicable |
| `Decimal64` | no | not applicable |
| `Date32` | yes | via integer representation |
| `DateTime64` | yes | via integer representation |
| `Bool` | no | not applicable |
| `String` | no | not applicable |
| `UUID` | no | not applicable |
| `LowCardinality(String)` | no | not applicable |

## VIII.31.4 `DoubleDelta`

-   **Best for:** regular-interval timestamps.
-   **Layout:** first value, first delta, zigzag delta-of-delta → BitPack.
-   **Decode strategy:** two-level prefix sum.
-   **Applicable families:** int,temporal.
-   **Format test:** golden files `tests/format/codec/doubledelta/v1/*.bin` decoded by every release (backward compatibility, Part IV §54).
-   **Fuzzing:** `cargo fuzz run codec_doubledelta_decode` — decoder MUST reject malformed input with an error, never panic or read out of bounds; corpus kept in repo.

## VIII.31.5 `RLE`

-   **Best for:** long runs (sorted low-cardinality, flags).
-   **Layout:** (value, run_length u32) pairs, run lengths BitPacked.
-   **Decode strategy:** vectorized fill; count/sum evaluated on runs directly.
-   **Applicable families:** int,uint,temporal,bool,dict,string.
-   **Format test:** golden files `tests/format/codec/rle/v1/*.bin` decoded by every release (backward compatibility, Part IV §54).
-   **Fuzzing:** `cargo fuzz run codec_rle_decode` — decoder MUST reject malformed input with an error, never panic or read out of bounds; corpus kept in repo.

|---|---|---|
| `Int32` | yes | — |

## VIII.31.6 `Dictionary`

-   **Best for:** low/medium cardinality values.
-   **Layout:** per-part dictionary (sorted for order-preserving codes) + BitPacked codes.
-   **Decode strategy:** gather from dictionary; predicates evaluated on codes.
-   **Applicable families:** int,uint,float,decimal,string,fixedstr.
-   **Format test:** golden files `tests/format/codec/dictionary/v1/*.bin` decoded by every release (backward compatibility, Part IV §54).
-   **Fuzzing:** `cargo fuzz run codec_dictionary_decode` — decoder MUST reject malformed input with an error, never panic or read out of bounds; corpus kept in repo.

## VIII.31.7 `Gorilla`

-   **Best for:** slowly varying floats (metrics).
-   **Layout:** XOR with previous, leading/trailing zero encoding, bit stream.
-   **Decode strategy:** sequential; 4-way interleaved streams to restore ILP.
-   **Applicable families:** float.
-   **Format test:** golden files `tests/format/codec/gorilla/v1/*.bin` decoded by every release (backward compatibility, Part IV §54).
-   **Fuzzing:** `cargo fuzz run codec_gorilla_decode` — decoder MUST reject malformed input with an error, never panic or read out of bounds; corpus kept in repo.

## VIII.31.8 `ALP`

-   **Best for:** decimal-like doubles (prices, measurements).
-   **Layout:** per-vector exponent/factor; doubles → integers → FOR+BitPack; exceptions list.
-   **Decode strategy:** vectorized integer decode then multiply; exceptions patched.
-   **Applicable families:** float.
-   **Format test:** golden files `tests/format/codec/alp/v1/*.bin` decoded by every release (backward compatibility, Part IV §54).
-   **Fuzzing:** `cargo fuzz run codec_alp_decode` — decoder MUST reject malformed input with an error, never panic or read out of bounds; corpus kept in repo.

## VIII.31.9 `FSST`

-   **Best for:** strings with repeated substrings (URLs, logs).
-   **Layout:** symbol table (≤ 255 symbols ≤ 8 B) + code stream; random access per string.
-   **Decode strategy:** table lookup decode; equality on compressed form possible.
-   **Applicable families:** string.
-   **Format test:** golden files `tests/format/codec/fsst/v1/*.bin` decoded by every release (backward compatibility, Part IV §54).
-   **Fuzzing:** `cargo fuzz run codec_fsst_decode` — decoder MUST reject malformed input with an error, never panic or read out of bounds; corpus kept in repo.

-   **Decode strategy:** library decode; level chosen per preset.
