# IX.34 Query pattern cookbook

59 common analytical patterns and the architectural mechanism StrataDB MUST use to make each fast. This is both user documentation (schema and query design guidance) and an engineering checklist: each pattern has a benchmark in the catalog or in IX.39 and a golden plan.

| # | Pattern | Shape | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| P-01 | Count rows in last N minutes for one key | key-prefix + time range on sort key | primary key range; count from granule row counts for fully-covered granules |
| P-02 | Dashboard time series per service | GROUP BY time bucket, service over hours/days | aggregate projection per minute; partial-result cache per part |
| P-03 | Top N by count | GROUP BY low-card ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT N | dictionary-code aggregation + heap |
| P-04 | Top N by count, high cardinality | GROUP BY user_id ... LIMIT N | two-level agg; approximate topK if allowed |
| P-05 | Exact distinct count, high cardinality | count(DISTINCT x) | two-level hash set; spill; suggest uniq for dashboards |
| P-06 | Percentiles | quantile(p)(x) | t-digest states; aggregate projection with states |
| P-07 | Latest value per series | argMax(value, ts) GROUP BY series | memtable latest index + ReplacingMergeTree or projection ORDER BY series, ts DESC |
| P-08 | Point lookup by non-key id | WHERE trace_id = ... | re-sorted projection on trace_id or Bloom skip index |
| P-09 | Search logs for token in time window | hasToken + ts range ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT | token index + reverse read-in-order + early stop |
| P-10 | Substring search without index | LIKE '%x%' | SIMD memmem scan; ngram Bloom index if frequent |
| P-11 | Regex extraction | extract(msg, re) | literal prefilter; RE2-class engine |
| P-12 | Join fact with small dimension | fact JOIN dim ON key | dim builds; runtime Bloom filter into fact scan |
| P-13 | Join two large tables on key | big JOIN big | co-located shards or radix-partitioned hash join; grace spill |
| P-14 | Join on sorted keys | both tables sorted by join key | merge join, no hash table |
| P-15 | Semi join filter | WHERE x IN (SELECT ...) | hash set + runtime filter + key-range pruning if x is key |
| P-16 | Anti join | NOT IN / NOT EXISTS | null-aware anti join |
| P-17 | Funnel analysis | windowFunnel per user | sort by (user, ts) sort key; streaming per user |
| P-18 | Retention cohorts | retention(...) GROUP BY cohort | pre-aggregated daily active users MV |
| P-19 | Sessionization | window over user ordered by ts | PARTITION BY user streaming window when sorted |
| P-20 | Rolling averages | avg OVER (ROWS N PRECEDING) | sliding window add/remove |
| P-21 | Rank within groups | row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY x) <= k | WindowToTopK rule |
| P-22 | Deduplicated latest rows | SELECT ... FINAL | parallel FINAL by key range; skip non-overlapping parts |
| P-23 | Upserts | frequent updates by key | ReplacingMergeTree with version; avoid mutations |
| P-24 | GDPR erase | DELETE WHERE user_id = ... | lightweight delete mask; physical removal at merge |
| P-25 | Bulk correction | UPDATE large subset | mutation (rewrite affected parts) scheduled off-peak |
| P-26 | Rollup table maintenance | hourly rollups | incremental MV into AggregatingMergeTree |
| P-27 | Downsampling time series | INSERT SELECT per hour | streaming aggregation reading in order |
| P-28 | Wide table, few columns queried | SELECT a, b FROM 200-col table | wide parts; column pruning; consider column groups / tiering |
| P-29 | Semi-structured attributes | JSON fields queried by path | JSON typed sub-columns |
| P-30 | Key-value attributes | Map(String,String) lookups | bucketed map sub-columns for top keys |
| P-31 | Many small inserts | 1 row per request from many clients | async insert buffers |
| P-32 | Backfill historical data | load years of data | bulk load path bypassing WAL; partition-parallel |
| P-33 | Late-arriving data | events hours late | insert into older partitions; merge planner per partition |
| P-34 | Retention | keep 30 days | TTL by partition drop (metadata) rather than row TTL |
| P-35 | Tiered retention | hot 7 d, cold 1 y | TTL MOVE to object storage; metadata stays local |
| P-36 | Sampling for exploration | approximate answers fast | SAMPLE with sampling key |
| P-37 | Approximate dashboards | speed over exactness | uniqHLL12, quantileTDigest, projections |
| P-38 | Multi-tenant isolation | tenant_id in every query | tenant_id first in sort key; per-tenant quotas |
| P-39 | Hot tenant | one tenant dominates | tenant quota; skew-aware aggregation; shard split |
| P-40 | Vector similarity search | ORDER BY distance LIMIT k | HNSW index with pre-filter bitmap; exact SIMD fallback |
| P-41 | Geo radius search | distance < r | geohash/H3 in sort key + bounding-box prefilter |
| P-42 | IP range filter | isIPAddressInRange | IPv4 as UInt32 range pruning |
| P-43 | Exports | SELECT large result to client | native/Arrow format; compression; streaming backpressure |
| P-44 | BI tool queries | repetitive generated SQL | plan cache + result cache + MV rewrite |
| P-45 | Ad-hoc exploration | unpredictable queries | good sort key + skip indexes + parallel scan |
| P-46 | Alerting queries every 10 s | same query repeated | partial-result cache; tiny time window pruning |
| P-47 | Cross-table reporting | union of tables | UNION ALL with per-branch pushdown |
| P-48 | Large GROUP BY exceeding memory | 1e9 groups | external aggregation (spill) or sketch |
| P-49 | Large ORDER BY | sort 1e10 rows | external sort; or read-in-order if key matches |
| P-50 | Distinct values listing | SELECT DISTINCT x | dictionary scan for LowCardinality; set skip index |
| P-51 | Min/max of a column | SELECT max(ts) | from part statistics |
| P-52 | Count by partition | count() GROUP BY partition key | metadata only |
| P-53 | Existence check | SELECT 1 WHERE ... LIMIT 1 | early stop at first match; index-first |
| P-54 | Histogram of values | histogram(n)(x) | single pass sketch |
| P-55 | Correlation analysis | corr(x, y) | single pass Welford state |
| P-56 | Time-zone reporting | GROUP BY toStartOfDay(ts, tz) | timezone LUT; projection per tz if dominant |
| P-57 | Calendar joins | join with date dimension | replace with date functions when possible |
| P-58 | Change data capture ingest | CDC stream with deletes | ReplacingMergeTree with is_deleted flag |
| P-59 | Event-time ordering | ORDER BY ts LIMIT 100 recent | reverse read-in-order on ts within key prefix |

### P-01: Count rows in last N minutes for one key

-   **Mechanism:** primary key range; count from granule row counts for fully-covered granules.

-   **Verification:** benchmark `PAT-01` and golden plan asserting the mechanism is used.

-   **Schema advice surfaced by advisor:** when the fingerprint matching this shape exceeds 1% of cluster CPU, the advisor suggests the mechanism above with estimated savings.
-   **Verification:** benchmark `PAT-50` and golden plan asserting the mechanism is used.

### P-51: Min/max of a column
-   **Query shape:** SELECT max(ts).
-   **Mechanism:** from part statistics.
-   **Schema advice surfaced by advisor:** when the fingerprint matching this shape exceeds 1% of cluster CPU, the advisor suggests the mechanism above with estimated savings.
-   **Verification:** benchmark `PAT-51` and golden plan asserting the mechanism is used.

### P-52: Count by partition
-   **Query shape:** count() GROUP BY partition key.
-   **Mechanism:** metadata only.
-   **Schema advice surfaced by advisor:** when the fingerprint matching this shape exceeds 1% of cluster CPU, the advisor suggests the mechanism above with estimated savings.
-   **Verification:** benchmark `PAT-52` and golden plan asserting the mechanism is used.

### P-53: Existence check
-   **Query shape:** SELECT 1 WHERE ... LIMIT 1.
-   **Mechanism:** early stop at first match; index-first.
-   **Schema advice surfaced by advisor:** when the fingerprint matching this shape exceeds 1% of cluster CPU, the advisor suggests the mechanism above with estimated savings.
-   **Verification:** benchmark `PAT-53` and golden plan asserting the mechanism is used.

### P-54: Histogram of values
-   **Query shape:** histogram(n)(x).
-   **Mechanism:** single pass sketch.
-   **Schema advice surfaced by advisor:** when the fingerprint matching this shape exceeds 1% of cluster CPU, the advisor suggests the mechanism above with estimated savings.
-   **Verification:** benchmark `PAT-54` and golden plan asserting the mechanism is used.

### P-55: Correlation analysis
-   **Query shape:** corr(x, y).
-   **Mechanism:** single pass Welford state.
-   **Schema advice surfaced by advisor:** when the fingerprint matching this shape exceeds 1% of cluster CPU, the advisor suggests the mechanism above with estimated savings.
-   **Verification:** benchmark `PAT-55` and golden plan asserting the mechanism is used.

### P-56: Time-zone reporting
-   **Query shape:** GROUP BY toStartOfDay(ts, tz).
-   **Mechanism:** timezone LUT; projection per tz if dominant.
-   **Schema advice surfaced by advisor:** when the fingerprint matching this shape exceeds 1% of cluster CPU, the advisor suggests the mechanism above with estimated savings.
-   **Verification:** benchmark `PAT-56` and golden plan asserting the mechanism is used.

### P-57: Calendar joins
-   **Query shape:** join with date dimension.
-   **Mechanism:** replace with date functions when possible.
-   **Schema advice surfaced by advisor:** when the fingerprint matching this shape exceeds 1% of cluster CPU, the advisor suggests the mechanism above with estimated savings.
-   **Verification:** benchmark `PAT-57` and golden plan asserting the mechanism is used.

### P-58: Change data capture ingest
-   **Query shape:** CDC stream with deletes.
-   **Mechanism:** ReplacingMergeTree with is_deleted flag.
-   **Schema advice surfaced by advisor:** when the fingerprint matching this shape exceeds 1% of cluster CPU, the advisor suggests the mechanism above with estimated savings.
-   **Verification:** benchmark `PAT-58` and golden plan asserting the mechanism is used.

### P-59: Event-time ordering
-   **Query shape:** ORDER BY ts LIMIT 100 recent.
-   **Mechanism:** reverse read-in-order on ts within key prefix.
-   **Schema advice surfaced by advisor:** when the fingerprint matching this shape exceeds 1% of cluster CPU, the advisor suggests the mechanism above with estimated savings.
-   **Verification:** benchmark `PAT-59` and golden plan asserting the mechanism is used.

# IX.35 Reference workload profiles

16 reference workloads with the recommended physical design. Each profile is shipped as an example (`examples/workloads/<name>/`) with schema DDL, a data generator, a query set, and a benchmark scenario, so architectural regressions are caught on realistic shapes, not only synthetic microbenchmarks.

## IX.35.1 Observability (traces/logs/metrics SaaS)

| Aspect | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Tables | events, logs, metrics |
| Sort key (main table) | `(tenant_id, service, ts)` |
| Partition | `toDate(ts)` |
| Projections / MVs | per-minute error/latency projection; trace_id projection |
| Indexes | token index on message; Bloom on trace_id |
| Settings & engine choices | async insert on; memtable.max_age_ms 500; TTL 30 d with tiering |
| Dominant performance concern | ingest rate, merges, log search |

-   **Benchmark scenario:** `scenarios/workloads/01.toml` with ingest at 50% of capacity plus the query set at target concurrency; acceptance = query p99 within profile target and no merge backlog growth over 1 h.
-   **Schema anti-patterns to flag:** partition key finer than a day for this workload; sort key starting with a high-cardinality column; JSON blobs where typed sub-columns apply; missing tenant/key prefix in sort key.

|---|---|

| Projections / MVs | daily active users MV; funnel helper projection ORDER BY (project_id, user_id, ts) |

# IX.36 Part IX settings and metrics

## IX.36.1 Settings

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `projection.enabled` | true | Use projections in query planning |
| `projection.build_on_merge` | true | Rebuild missing projections during merges |
| `projection.max_per_table` | 16 | Cap on projections per table |
| `mv.synchronous` | false | Run MV transform inside insert before ack |
| `mv.max_lag_ms_for_rewrite` | 60000 | Freshness required for automatic MV rewrite |
| `mv.parallel_transforms` | 4 | Parallel MV transforms per insert block |
| `json.max_dynamic_paths` | 1024 | Typed sub-column paths per JSON column |
| `json.infer_types` | true | Infer sub-column types at ingest |
| `map.bucket_count` | 16 | Buckets for Map sub-columns |
| `map.top_keys_as_columns` | 32 | Keys promoted to dedicated sub-columns |
| `delete.lightweight` | true | DELETE uses masks |
| `delete.mask_merge_threshold` | 0.2 | Fraction deleted that triggers physical removal merge |
| `patch_parts.enabled` | false | On-the-fly patch parts for point updates |
| `final.parallel_ranges` | auto | Key ranges for parallel FINAL |
| `final.skip_non_overlapping` | true | Skip query-time merge for non-overlapping parts |
| `cache.partial_results` | false | Partial aggregate cache per part |
| `cache.partial_results_bytes` | 5% RAM | Partial result cache size |
| `index.effectiveness_tracking` | true | Track skip index usefulness |
| `index.inverted.tokenizer` | unicode_words | Default tokenizer |
| `index.inverted.postings_codec` | roaring | Postings compression |
| `index.vector.type` | hnsw | Default vector index |
| `index.vector.hnsw_m` | 16 | HNSW degree |
| `index.vector.ef_search` | 64 | HNSW search breadth |
| `ingest.max_partitions_per_insert_block` | 100 | Reject inserts touching too many partitions |
| `ingest.bulk_bypass_wal` | true | Bulk loads write parts directly |
| `ingest.allow_errors_ratio` | 0 | Fraction of bad rows tolerated |
| `exec.compact_threshold` | 0.25 | Selection density below which batches compact |
| `exec.pipeline_template_cache` | true | Cache compiled pipeline templates |
| `exec.adaptive_build_swap` | true | Allow join build/probe role reversal |
| `tier.move_bytes_per_sec` | 100MiB | Tier move rate limit |
| `tier.keep_metadata_local` | true | Keep metadata of remote parts on local NVMe |
| `replication.max_lag_ms` | 1000 | Replica freshness target |
| `distributed.broadcast_max_bytes` | 64MiB | Broadcast join threshold |
| `advisor.enabled` | true | Workload advisor recommendations |
| `advisor.min_cpu_share` | 0.01 | Fingerprint CPU share to consider |

## IX.36.2 Metrics

| Metric | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `strata_projection_hits_total` | counter | queries answered (partly) by projections |
| `strata_projection_build_seconds` | histogram | projection build time per part |
| `strata_mv_lag_seconds` | gauge | async MV lag |
| `strata_mv_rows_total` | counter | rows written by MVs |
| `strata_json_dynamic_paths` | gauge | typed JSON paths per column |
| `strata_delete_mask_rows` | gauge | rows masked but not yet removed |
| `strata_final_overlapping_parts` | histogram | overlapping parts merged at query time |
| `strata_partial_cache_hit_ratio` | gauge | partial result cache part-hit ratio |
| `strata_index_skip_ratio` | histogram | granules skipped / examined per index |

# IX.37 Fault-injection cells for Part IX mechanisms

Total additional cells: **113**.

Extends VIII.24 to the transition points introduced by Part IX. Same harness, same verification steps.

## IX.37.1 PROJ-BUILD — projection build within flush/merge

| Fault | Required outcome |
|---|---|
| `CRASH-BEFORE` | recover to state before the step; invariant: part never ACTIVE without projection or explicit 'missing' marker. |
| `CRASH-AFTER` | recover to state after the step (if it was durable) or before; invariant: part never ACTIVE without projection or explicit 'missing' marker. |
| `POWER-LOSS` | only fsynced data survives; invariant holds; invariant: part never ACTIVE without projection or explicit 'missing' marker. |
| `EIO-WRITE` | operation fails; no partial publish; error surfaced with path; invariant: part never ACTIVE without projection or explicit 'missing' marker. |
| `EIO-FSYNC` | treat data as lost; do not retry-and-trust; fail operation (WAL: read-only mode); invariant: part never ACTIVE without projection or explicit 'missing' marker. |
| `ENOSPC` | operation fails cleanly; temp files removed; system enters space-protection mode; invariant: part never ACTIVE without projection or explicit 'missing' marker. |
| `SHORT-WRITE` | remainder resubmitted; or failure propagated; invariant: part never ACTIVE without projection or explicit 'missing' marker. |
| `TORN-SECTOR` | CRC/checksum detects; torn tail truncated or part rejected; invariant: part never ACTIVE without projection or explicit 'missing' marker. |
| `BITFLIP-READ` | checksum mismatch detected; not returned to client; scrub scheduled; invariant: part never ACTIVE without projection or explicit 'missing' marker. |
| `LATENCY-1S` | no correctness change; timeouts and backpressure behave; metrics show latency; invariant: part never ACTIVE without projection or explicit 'missing' marker. |
| `RENAME-FAIL` | temp state cleaned; operation fails; retry safe; invariant: part never ACTIVE without projection or explicit 'missing' marker. |
| `CONCURRENT-QUERY` | query sees consistent snapshot throughout; files not deleted under it; invariant: part never ACTIVE without projection or explicit 'missing' marker. |

# IX.38 Performance tests for Part IX subsystems

Applies the 15 test dimensions of VIII.26 to 12 Part IX subsystems. Each test additionally asserts **result equivalence** with the base plan (no projection, no MV, no index, no cache).

## IX.38.1 Projections (`PROJ`)

### PT-PROJ-BASELINE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** HW-REF-1, SF=1 dataset relevant to the subsystem, default settings, warm caches unless the subsystem is I/O.
-   **Pass:** Correct baseline throughput on HW-REF-1 at SF=1; establishes ledger value. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-SCALING-CORES
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** cpuset restricted per step (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers); same dataset; SMT disabled for the sweep.
-   **Pass:** Throughput at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers; efficiency ≥ 80% up to 16 workers for parallelizable work. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-SCALING-DATA
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** SF 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 with identical schema and distributions.
-   **Pass:** Behavior at SF 0.01 → 10; cost per row must stay within 1.3× across scale. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-SKEW
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** datasets regenerated with Zipf exponent 0, 1.1, 2.0 on the dominant key.
-   **Pass:** Zipf s ∈ {0, 1.1, 2.0} on the dominant key; no worker > 2× median busy time. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-MEMORY-LIMIT
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** max_memory_usage set to 25% of the peak observed in the baseline run; spill enabled.
-   **Pass:** Run with memory limit at 25% of unconstrained peak; must spill or fail cleanly, never OOM. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-CANCELLATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** 1,000 runs each cancelled at a uniformly random time between 0 and the baseline duration.
-   **Pass:** Cancel at random points; all resources released within 10 ms p99; no leaked reservations. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-CONCURRENCY
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Setup:** 64 concurrent clients, open-loop arrival at 80% of measured saturation.
-   **Pass:** 64 concurrent instances; aggregate throughput ≥ 0.8× single-instance × min(64, cores). Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-COLD-VS-WARM
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** run after `drop_caches` and engine cache clear, then immediately again.
-   **Pass:** Report both; cold must reach ≥ 85% of device bandwidth where I/O-bound. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-ISA-TIERS
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** `STRATA_FORCE_ISA` set to scalar, x86-64-v3, x86-64-v4 on x86 runners and neon / sve on ARM runners.
-   **Pass:** Run with dispatch forced to scalar, v3, v4, NEON; results identical; speedups recorded. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-ALLOCATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** counting global allocator build (`--features alloc-count`), 10,000 batches after 100-batch warmup.
-   **Pass:** Counting allocator: steady-state allocations per batch equals documented value (usually 0). Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-LONG-RUN
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Setup:** 6-hour soak with mixed load representative of the subsystem.
-   **Pass:** 6-hour soak; no throughput decay > 10%, no RSS growth > 5% after warmup. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-REGRESSION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** same scenario as baseline on the dedicated runner; compared to rolling 10-run window.
-   **Pass:** Compared against rolling baseline (STRATA-SYS-19-005); blocks merge on significant regression. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-NOISY-NEIGHBOR
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Setup:** `stress-ng --cpu N --io 4 --vm 2` in a sibling cgroup with equal weight.
-   **Pass:** Run alongside a CPU+IO hog in another cgroup; degradation documented and bounded by quotas. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-FAILURE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** fault from VIII.24 injected for 30 s then cleared.
-   **Pass:** Inject relevant I/O faults from VIII.24; performance recovers to baseline within 60 s after fault clears. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PROJ-OBSERVABILITY
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** baseline scenario with metrics scrape every 1 s and EXPLAIN ANALYZE enabled.
-   **Pass:** Every metric/EXPLAIN counter for the subsystem is populated and plausible (cross-checked against PMU or OS counters). Results identical to the base plan.

-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** same scenario as baseline on the dedicated runner; compared to rolling 10-run window.
-   **Pass:** Compared against rolling baseline (STRATA-SYS-19-005); blocks merge on significant regression. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-INV-NOISY-NEIGHBOR
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Setup:** `stress-ng --cpu N --io 4 --vm 2` in a sibling cgroup with equal weight.
-   **Pass:** Run alongside a CPU+IO hog in another cgroup; degradation documented and bounded by quotas. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-INV-FAILURE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** fault from VIII.24 injected for 30 s then cleared.
-   **Pass:** Inject relevant I/O faults from VIII.24; performance recovers to baseline within 60 s after fault clears. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-INV-OBSERVABILITY
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** baseline scenario with metrics scrape every 1 s and EXPLAIN ANALYZE enabled.
-   **Pass:** Every metric/EXPLAIN counter for the subsystem is populated and plausible (cross-checked against PMU or OS counters). Results identical to the base plan.

## IX.38.4 Vector index (`VEC`)

### PT-VEC-BASELINE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** HW-REF-1, SF=1 dataset relevant to the subsystem, default settings, warm caches unless the subsystem is I/O.
-   **Pass:** Correct baseline throughput on HW-REF-1 at SF=1; establishes ledger value. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-SCALING-CORES
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** cpuset restricted per step (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers); same dataset; SMT disabled for the sweep.
-   **Pass:** Throughput at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers; efficiency ≥ 80% up to 16 workers for parallelizable work. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-SCALING-DATA
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** SF 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 with identical schema and distributions.
-   **Pass:** Behavior at SF 0.01 → 10; cost per row must stay within 1.3× across scale. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-SKEW
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** datasets regenerated with Zipf exponent 0, 1.1, 2.0 on the dominant key.
-   **Pass:** Zipf s ∈ {0, 1.1, 2.0} on the dominant key; no worker > 2× median busy time. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-MEMORY-LIMIT
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** max_memory_usage set to 25% of the peak observed in the baseline run; spill enabled.
-   **Pass:** Run with memory limit at 25% of unconstrained peak; must spill or fail cleanly, never OOM. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-CANCELLATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** 1,000 runs each cancelled at a uniformly random time between 0 and the baseline duration.
-   **Pass:** Cancel at random points; all resources released within 10 ms p99; no leaked reservations. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-CONCURRENCY
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Setup:** 64 concurrent clients, open-loop arrival at 80% of measured saturation.
-   **Pass:** 64 concurrent instances; aggregate throughput ≥ 0.8× single-instance × min(64, cores). Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-COLD-VS-WARM
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** run after `drop_caches` and engine cache clear, then immediately again.
-   **Pass:** Report both; cold must reach ≥ 85% of device bandwidth where I/O-bound. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-ISA-TIERS
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** `STRATA_FORCE_ISA` set to scalar, x86-64-v3, x86-64-v4 on x86 runners and neon / sve on ARM runners.
-   **Pass:** Run with dispatch forced to scalar, v3, v4, NEON; results identical; speedups recorded. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-ALLOCATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** counting global allocator build (`--features alloc-count`), 10,000 batches after 100-batch warmup.
-   **Pass:** Counting allocator: steady-state allocations per batch equals documented value (usually 0). Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-LONG-RUN
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Setup:** 6-hour soak with mixed load representative of the subsystem.
-   **Pass:** 6-hour soak; no throughput decay > 10%, no RSS growth > 5% after warmup. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-REGRESSION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** same scenario as baseline on the dedicated runner; compared to rolling 10-run window.
-   **Pass:** Compared against rolling baseline (STRATA-SYS-19-005); blocks merge on significant regression. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-NOISY-NEIGHBOR
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Setup:** `stress-ng --cpu N --io 4 --vm 2` in a sibling cgroup with equal weight.
-   **Pass:** Run alongside a CPU+IO hog in another cgroup; degradation documented and bounded by quotas. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-FAILURE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** fault from VIII.24 injected for 30 s then cleared.
-   **Pass:** Inject relevant I/O faults from VIII.24; performance recovers to baseline within 60 s after fault clears. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-VEC-OBSERVABILITY
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** baseline scenario with metrics scrape every 1 s and EXPLAIN ANALYZE enabled.
-   **Pass:** Every metric/EXPLAIN counter for the subsystem is populated and plausible (cross-checked against PMU or OS counters). Results identical to the base plan.

-   **Pass:** Run with memory limit at 25% of unconstrained peak; must spill or fail cleanly, never OOM. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PCACHE-CANCELLATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** 1,000 runs each cancelled at a uniformly random time between 0 and the baseline duration.
-   **Pass:** Cancel at random points; all resources released within 10 ms p99; no leaked reservations. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PCACHE-CONCURRENCY
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Setup:** 64 concurrent clients, open-loop arrival at 80% of measured saturation.
-   **Pass:** 64 concurrent instances; aggregate throughput ≥ 0.8× single-instance × min(64, cores). Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PCACHE-COLD-VS-WARM
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** run after `drop_caches` and engine cache clear, then immediately again.
-   **Pass:** Report both; cold must reach ≥ 85% of device bandwidth where I/O-bound. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PCACHE-ISA-TIERS
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** `STRATA_FORCE_ISA` set to scalar, x86-64-v3, x86-64-v4 on x86 runners and neon / sve on ARM runners.
-   **Pass:** Run with dispatch forced to scalar, v3, v4, NEON; results identical; speedups recorded. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PCACHE-ALLOCATION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** counting global allocator build (`--features alloc-count`), 10,000 batches after 100-batch warmup.
-   **Pass:** Counting allocator: steady-state allocations per batch equals documented value (usually 0). Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PCACHE-LONG-RUN
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Setup:** 6-hour soak with mixed load representative of the subsystem.
-   **Pass:** 6-hour soak; no throughput decay > 10%, no RSS growth > 5% after warmup. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PCACHE-REGRESSION
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** same scenario as baseline on the dedicated runner; compared to rolling 10-run window.
-   **Pass:** Compared against rolling baseline (STRATA-SYS-19-005); blocks merge on significant regression. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PCACHE-NOISY-NEIGHBOR
-   **Level:** SHOULD. **Setup:** `stress-ng --cpu N --io 4 --vm 2` in a sibling cgroup with equal weight.
-   **Pass:** Run alongside a CPU+IO hog in another cgroup; degradation documented and bounded by quotas. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PCACHE-FAILURE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** fault from VIII.24 injected for 30 s then cleared.
-   **Pass:** Inject relevant I/O faults from VIII.24; performance recovers to baseline within 60 s after fault clears. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-PCACHE-OBSERVABILITY
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** baseline scenario with metrics scrape every 1 s and EXPLAIN ANALYZE enabled.
-   **Pass:** Every metric/EXPLAIN counter for the subsystem is populated and plausible (cross-checked against PMU or OS counters). Results identical to the base plan.

## IX.38.11 Bulk load path (`BULK`)

### PT-BULK-BASELINE
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** HW-REF-1, SF=1 dataset relevant to the subsystem, default settings, warm caches unless the subsystem is I/O.
-   **Pass:** Correct baseline throughput on HW-REF-1 at SF=1; establishes ledger value. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-BULK-SCALING-CORES
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** cpuset restricted per step (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers); same dataset; SMT disabled for the sweep.
-   **Pass:** Throughput at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 28 workers; efficiency ≥ 80% up to 16 workers for parallelizable work. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-BULK-SCALING-DATA
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** SF 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 with identical schema and distributions.
-   **Pass:** Behavior at SF 0.01 → 10; cost per row must stay within 1.3× across scale. Results identical to the base plan.

### PT-BULK-SKEW
-   **Level:** MUST. **Setup:** datasets regenerated with Zipf exponent 0, 1.1, 2.0 on the dominant key.
-   **Pass:** Zipf s ∈ {0, 1.1, 2.0} on the dominant key; no worker > 2× median busy time. Results identical to the base plan.

# IX.39 Benchmark queries for Part IX mechanisms

Total: **87** query variants.

Each query runs with the mechanism enabled and disabled; the report shows speedup, extra storage, extra ingest CPU, and result equality.

## projection-agg

### Q-IX-001 (projection-agg, tenant 1, window 15 MINUTE)
-   **Required plan property:** aggregate projection used; boundary minutes from base.
-   **Report:** speedup on/off, bytes read on/off, storage overhead, ingest CPU overhead.

```sql
SELECT service, count(), avg(duration_ms) FROM events WHERE tenant_id = 1 AND ts >= now() - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE GROUP BY service;
```

# IX.41 Reference workload schemas and query sets

Workloads: **10**, queries: **50**.

Concrete DDL and query sets for the reference workloads in IX.35. These are executable examples that apply Part IX layout rules (sort key prefix, LowCardinality, typed JSON/Map, projections, skip indexes, TTL tiering). Each query lists the expected dominant mechanism; the benchmark harness asserts it in the plan.

## IX.41.1 `observability`

```sql
CREATE TABLE events
(
    tenant_id UInt32,
    service LowCardinality(String),
    ts DateTime64(6),
    trace_id FixedString(16),
    span_id UInt64,
    duration_ms Float32,
    status_code UInt16,
    attributes Map(LowCardinality(String), String),
    message String,
    INDEX idx_trace trace_id TYPE bloom_filter(0.01) GRANULARITY 4,
    INDEX idx_msg message TYPE tokenbf(32768, 3, 0) GRANULARITY 4,
    PROJECTION p_min (SELECT tenant_id, service, toStartOfMinute(ts) m, count(), avgState(duration_ms), quantileTDigestState(duration_ms) GROUP BY tenant_id, service, m)
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
PARTITION BY toDate(ts)
ORDER BY (tenant_id, service, ts)
TTL toDateTime(ts) + INTERVAL 30 DAY
SETTINGS compression_preset = 'balanced';
```

### W-OBSERVABILITY-01
-   **Expected mechanism:** primary-key prefix + time pruning + aggregation; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT service, count() FROM events WHERE tenant_id = 7 AND ts >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR AND status_code >= 500 GROUP BY service ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10;
```

### W-OBSERVABILITY-02
-   **Expected mechanism:** projection or read-in-order; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT toStartOfMinute(ts) m, quantileTDigest(0.99)(duration_ms) FROM events WHERE tenant_id = 7 AND service = 'api' AND ts >= now() - INTERVAL 6 HOUR GROUP BY m ORDER BY m;
```

### W-OBSERVABILITY-03
-   **Expected mechanism:** skip index / projection point lookup; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT * FROM events WHERE tenant_id = 7 AND trace_id = unhex('4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736');
```

### W-OBSERVABILITY-04
-   **Expected mechanism:** token/ngram index + early stop; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT ts, message FROM events WHERE tenant_id = 7 AND hasToken(message, 'timeout') AND ts >= now() - INTERVAL 1 DAY ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50;
```

### W-OBSERVABILITY-05
-   **Expected mechanism:** sub-column read + aggregation; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT attributes['http.route'] r, count(), avg(duration_ms) FROM events WHERE tenant_id = 7 AND ts >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR GROUP BY r ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20;
```

## IX.41.2 `product_analytics`

```sql
CREATE TABLE app_events
(
    project_id UInt32,
    event_name LowCardinality(String),
    ts DateTime,
    user_id UInt64,
    session_id UInt64,
    country LowCardinality(String),
    properties JSON,
    PROJECTION p_user (SELECT project_id, user_id, ts, event_name ORDER BY project_id, user_id, ts)
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
PARTITION BY toYYYYMM(ts)
ORDER BY (project_id, event_name, ts, user_id)
SETTINGS compression_preset = 'balanced';
```

### W-PRODUCT_ANALYTICS-01
-   **Expected mechanism:** primary-key prefix + time pruning + aggregation; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT toDate(ts) d, uniq(user_id) FROM app_events WHERE project_id = 3 AND ts >= today() - 30 GROUP BY d ORDER BY d;
```

### W-PRODUCT_ANALYTICS-02
-   **Expected mechanism:** projection or read-in-order; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT level, count() FROM (SELECT user_id, windowFunnel(86400)(ts, event_name = 'view', event_name = 'cart', event_name = 'buy') level FROM app_events WHERE project_id = 3 AND ts >= today() - 7 GROUP BY user_id) GROUP BY level ORDER BY level;
```

### W-PRODUCT_ANALYTICS-03
-   **Expected mechanism:** skip index / projection point lookup; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT properties.utm.source s, count() FROM app_events WHERE project_id = 3 AND event_name = 'signup' AND ts >= today() - 30 GROUP BY s ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 20;
```

### W-PRODUCT_ANALYTICS-04
-   **Expected mechanism:** token/ngram index + early stop; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT country, uniqExact(user_id) FROM app_events WHERE project_id = 3 AND ts >= today() - 1 GROUP BY country ORDER BY 2 DESC;
```

### W-PRODUCT_ANALYTICS-05
-   **Expected mechanism:** sub-column read + aggregation; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT retention(event_name = 'signup' AND toDate(ts) = today() - 7, toDate(ts) = today() - 6, toDate(ts) = today() - 1) r FROM app_events WHERE project_id = 3 GROUP BY user_id;
```

## IX.41.3 `adtech`

```sql
CREATE TABLE impressions
(
    advertiser_id UInt32,
    campaign_id UInt32,
    ts DateTime,
    request_id UUID,
    site LowCardinality(String),
    cost_micros UInt64,
    clicked UInt8,
    INDEX idx_req request_id TYPE bloom_filter(0.01) GRANULARITY 4
)
ENGINE = MergeTree
PARTITION BY toDate(ts)
ORDER BY (advertiser_id, campaign_id, ts)
TTL ts + INTERVAL 90 DAY
SETTINGS compression_preset = 'balanced';
```

### W-ADTECH-01
-   **Expected mechanism:** primary-key prefix + time pruning + aggregation; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT campaign_id, count(), sum(clicked), sum(cost_micros) / 1e6 FROM impressions WHERE advertiser_id = 11 AND ts >= today() GROUP BY campaign_id;
```

### W-ADTECH-02
-   **Expected mechanism:** projection or read-in-order; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT site, sum(clicked) / count() ctr FROM impressions WHERE advertiser_id = 11 AND ts >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR GROUP BY site HAVING count() > 1000 ORDER BY ctr DESC LIMIT 20;
```

### W-ADTECH-03
-   **Expected mechanism:** skip index / projection point lookup; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT toStartOfHour(ts) h, sum(cost_micros) FROM impressions WHERE advertiser_id = 11 AND ts >= today() - 7 GROUP BY h ORDER BY h;
```

### W-ADTECH-04
-   **Expected mechanism:** token/ngram index + early stop; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT count() FROM impressions i JOIN clicks c ON c.request_id = i.request_id WHERE i.advertiser_id = 11 AND i.ts >= today();
```

### W-ADTECH-05
-   **Expected mechanism:** sub-column read + aggregation; verified against EXPLAIN.
-   **Run modes:** cold / warm, concurrency 1 / 16 / 64, during 50% ingest load.

```sql
SELECT uniqHLL12(request_id) FROM impressions WHERE ts >= today();
```

## IX.41.9 `netflow`


## IX.41.10 `cdc_replica`

```sql
CREATE TABLE users_replacing
(
    tenant_id UInt32,
    user_id UInt64,
    version UInt64,
    is_deleted UInt8,
    email String,
    plan LowCardinality(String),
    updated_at DateTime
)
ENGINE = ReplacingMergeTree(version, is_deleted)
ORDER BY (tenant_id, user_id)
SETTINGS compression_preset = 'balanced';
```

# IX.44 Golden plans for Part IX benchmark queries

Expected plan shapes for each query family in IX.39 (variants differ only by literals).

## projection-agg

```text
Output
└─ Aggregate(final) merge states
   └─ Union
      ├─ ProjectionScan(p_min) key range tenant, minute-aligned interior
      └─ TableScan(base) boundary minutes only, PREWHERE ts
```
-   **Asserted:** aggregate projection used; boundary minutes from base; result equals the plan with the mechanism disabled.

## projection-point

```text
Output
└─ ProjectionScan(by_trace) primary key = trace_id → 1–2 granules per part
   └─ LateMaterialize(base columns by row id)
```
-   **Asserted:** re-sorted projection by_trace used; result equals the plan with the mechanism disabled.

## mv-rewrite

```text
Output
└─ Aggregate(final) re-aggregate hourly states
   └─ TableScan(mv_hourly_target) hour range
```
-   **Asserted:** rewritten to hourly MV target; result equals the plan with the mechanism disabled.

## json-path

```text
Output
└─ Aggregate keys=c
   └─ TableScan(raw_json) cols=[ts, data.user.country (typed sub-column)]
```
-   **Asserted:** only sub-column data.user.country read; result equals the plan with the mechanism disabled.

## map-key

```text
Output
└─ Aggregate keys=r
   └─ TableScan(events) cols=[ts, attributes.bucket(region)]
```
-   **Asserted:** bucket sub-stream read; result equals the plan with the mechanism disabled.

## delete-masked

```text
Output
└─ Aggregate(count)
   └─ DeleteMaskApply (granules fully deleted skipped)
      └─ TableScan(events) key range tenant
```
-   **Asserted:** delete masks applied at granule and row level; result equals the plan with the mechanism disabled.

## final

```text
Output
└─ Aggregate(count)
   └─ FinalMerge parallel by key range (overlapping parts only)
      └─ TableScan(users_replacing) key range tenant
```
-   **Asserted:** parallel FINAL; non-overlapping parts skipped; result equals the plan with the mechanism disabled.

## vector

```text
Output
└─ TopK(10, distance)
   └─ VectorSearch(HNSW, allow-list bitmap from collection_id = t)
```
-   **Asserted:** HNSW with pre-filter; result equals the plan with the mechanism disabled.

## inverted

```text
Output
└─ Aggregate(count)
   └─ TextSearch(postings AND, galloping) → row ids
      └─ TableScan(logs) ts range, row-id filtered
```
-   **Asserted:** postings intersection, galloping; result equals the plan with the mechanism disabled.

## tiered

```text
Output
└─ Aggregate(count)
   └─ TableScan(events_archive) metadata local; ranged GET + hedging; local object cache
```
-   **Asserted:** metadata local; ranged GETs with hedging; result equals the plan with the mechanism disabled.

## pcache

```text
Output
└─ Aggregate(final) merges cached per-part states + fresh states
   ├─ PartialCacheLookup(unchanged parts)
   └─ Aggregate(partial) ← TableScan(new parts only)
```
-   **Asserted:** partial results reused for unchanged parts; result equals the plan with the mechanism disabled.

# IX.46 Index type catalog and applicability

| Index | Structure | Column types | Parameters | Accelerates | Size | Caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `minmax` | per N granules min and max | any ordered type | GRANULARITY 1–8 | range predicates on columns correlated with sort order | 2 × width per block | none |
| `set(k)` | distinct values if ≤ k else 'many' | any | k = 100–10,000 | equality/IN on low-cardinality per block | ≤ k values per block | none |
| `bloom_filter(fpr)` | split-block Bloom per block | any hashable | fpr 0.001–0.05 | equality/IN on high-cardinality | ~1.44·log2(1/fpr) bits per distinct | fpr |
| `tokenbf(size, hashes, seed)` | Bloom over tokens | String | size 4–64 KiB | hasToken, equality on tokens | size per block | tokenizer mismatch disables |
| `ngrambf_v1(n, size, hashes, seed)` | Bloom over n-grams | String | n = 3–4 | LIKE '%x%' with |x| ≥ n | size per block | short needles not accelerated |
| `inverted(tokenizer)` | row-level postings | String | tokenizer | full-text AND/OR, phrase (with positions) | proportional to tokens | build cost |
| `hnsw(m, ef)` | graph ANN | Vector(Float32, D) | m 8–48, ef 32–512 | nearest neighbours | ~(m·2·4 B + D·4 B) per vector | approximate |
| `ivf_pq(lists, subq)` | inverted file + product quantization | Vector | lists √n | memory-efficient ANN | subq bytes per vector | approximate |
| `projection (re-sorted)` | alternate sort order | columns subset | ORDER BY | point/range on secondary key | ≈ subset size | ingest + storage |
| `projection (aggregate)` | pre-aggregated states | aggregates | GROUP BY | dashboards | ≈ groups × states | ingest CPU |

## IX.46.1 Applicability matrix

| Index | `UInt64` | `Int32` | `Float64` | `Date32` | `DateTime64` | `String` | `LowCardinality(String)` | `UUID` | `IPv4` | `Vector(Float32, 768)` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `minmax` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — | ✓ | — |
| `set(k)` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| `bloom_filter(fpr)` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| `tokenbf(size, hashes, seed)` | — | — | — | — | — | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
| `ngrambf_v1(n, size, hashes, seed)` | — | — | — | — | — | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
| `inverted(tokenizer)` | — | — | — | — | — | ✓ | — | — | — | — |
| `hnsw(m, ef)` | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | ✓ |
| `ivf_pq(lists, subq)` | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | — | ✓ |
| `projection (re-sorted)` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| `projection (aggregate)` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — |

## IX.46.2 `minmax`

-   **Structure:** per N granules min and max. **Parameters:** GRANULARITY 1–8.
-   **Accelerates:** range predicates on columns correlated with sort order. **Size:** 2 × width per block. **Caveat:** none.
-   **Build:** during flush and merge; merge combines per-block structures without re-reading raw data where the structure permits (minmax, set, Bloom by OR of same-geometry filters, postings by remap).
-   **Evaluation cost target:** ≤ 1% of the scan cost it avoids on the index-effectiveness benchmark; otherwise the planner skips it.

## IX.46.3 `set(k)`

-   **Structure:** distinct values if ≤ k else 'many'. **Parameters:** k = 100–10,000.
-   **Accelerates:** equality/IN on low-cardinality per block. **Size:** ≤ k values per block. **Caveat:** none.
-   **Build:** during flush and merge; merge combines per-block structures without re-reading raw data where the structure permits (minmax, set, Bloom by OR of same-geometry filters, postings by remap).
-   **Evaluation cost target:** ≤ 1% of the scan cost it avoids on the index-effectiveness benchmark; otherwise the planner skips it.

## IX.46.4 `bloom_filter(fpr)`

-   **Structure:** split-block Bloom per block. **Parameters:** fpr 0.001–0.05.
-   **Accelerates:** equality/IN on high-cardinality. **Size:** ~1.44·log2(1/fpr) bits per distinct. **Caveat:** fpr.
-   **Build:** during flush and merge; merge combines per-block structures without re-reading raw data where the structure permits (minmax, set, Bloom by OR of same-geometry filters, postings by remap).
-   **Evaluation cost target:** ≤ 1% of the scan cost it avoids on the index-effectiveness benchmark; otherwise the planner skips it.

## IX.46.5 `tokenbf(size, hashes, seed)`

-   **Structure:** Bloom over tokens. **Parameters:** size 4–64 KiB.
-   **Accelerates:** hasToken, equality on tokens. **Size:** size per block. **Caveat:** tokenizer mismatch disables.
-   **Build:** during flush and merge; merge combines per-block structures without re-reading raw data where the structure permits (minmax, set, Bloom by OR of same-geometry filters, postings by remap).
-   **Evaluation cost target:** ≤ 1% of the scan cost it avoids on the index-effectiveness benchmark; otherwise the planner skips it.

## IX.46.6 `ngrambf_v1(n, size, hashes, seed)`

-   **Structure:** Bloom over n-grams. **Parameters:** n = 3–4.
-   **Accelerates:** LIKE '%x%' with |x| ≥ n. **Size:** size per block. **Caveat:** short needles not accelerated.
-   **Build:** during flush and merge; merge combines per-block structures without re-reading raw data where the structure permits (minmax, set, Bloom by OR of same-geometry filters, postings by remap).
-   **Evaluation cost target:** ≤ 1% of the scan cost it avoids on the index-effectiveness benchmark; otherwise the planner skips it.

# IX.48 Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Batch** | a set of column vectors (default 8,192 rows) processed together by operators |
| **Breaker** | operator that must consume all input before producing output (hash build, sort) |
| **CPR** | cycles per row — the primary CPU efficiency metric |
| **DOP** | degree of parallelism of a query or pipeline |
| **FINAL** | query-time merging for merge-on-read engines |
| **Granule** | smallest indexed unit of rows in a part (default 8,192) |
| **Group commit** | batching many WAL records into one fsync |
| **Late materialization** | reading payload columns only for rows that passed filters |
| **LSN** | log sequence number in the WAL |
| **Mark** | per-granule offset into a column file |
| **Memtable** | in-memory, queryable buffer of recent inserts |
| **Morsel** | schedulable unit of work (range of granules or rows) |
| **MV** | materialized view; insert-triggered transformation |
| **Normalized key** | memcmp-comparable byte encoding of sort keys |
| **Part** | immutable on-disk unit of sorted columnar data |
| **Partition** | lifecycle grouping of parts (e.g. by day) |
| **Pipeline** | chain of operators executed per morsel without materialization |
| **PREWHERE** | reading filter columns first to prune before payload |
| **Projection** | alternate physical representation stored inside parts |
| **Pruning** | skipping partitions, parts, granules that cannot match |
| **PSI** | Linux pressure stall information |
| **Q-error** | max(est/actual, actual/est) for cardinality estimates |
| **RCU** | read-copy-update; readers access immutable snapshots without locks |
| **Runtime filter** | filter derived from a join build applied to the probe scan |
| **Selection vector** | list or bitmap of active rows in a batch |
| **Skip index** | per-block summary allowing granules to be skipped |
| **Snapshot** | immutable view of the part set at query start |
| **Spill** | writing operator state to disk when memory is insufficient |
| **Two-level hash table** | hash table split into 256 sub-tables for parallel merge |
| **WA** | write amplification: physical bytes written / logical bytes ingested |
| **Zone map** | min/max per granule or block |
| **ALP** | adaptive lossless floating-point encoding |
| **FSST** | fast static symbol table string compression |
| **HNSW** | hierarchical navigable small world graph index |
| **Hedged request** | duplicate request sent after a latency threshold to cut tail latency |
| **Open-loop load** | requests sent on a schedule independent of responses |
| **PGO** | profile-guided optimization |
| **PLP** | power-loss protection on SSDs |
| **SLRU** | segmented LRU cache policy |
| **TinyLFU** | frequency-sketch cache admission policy |

# IX.49 Runbooks for Part IX mechanisms

## IX.49.1 Projection not used

**Diagnosis**

1.  EXPLAIN shows `projection: none` with reason
1.  check projection exists on all parts: system.projection_stats
1.  check query aggregates derivable from projection states

**Actions**

-   materialize projection on old parts (ALTER TABLE ... MATERIALIZE PROJECTION)
-   add missing state columns to projection

## IX.49.2 MV lag growing

**Diagnosis**

1.  strata_mv_lag_seconds
1.  MV transform CPU in system.materialized_views
1.  target table parts count

**Actions**

-   raise mv.parallel_transforms
-   simplify transform; avoid joins in incremental MV
-   check target merges

## IX.49.3 FINAL queries slow

**Diagnosis**

1.  strata_final_overlapping_parts
1.  merge backlog on the table

**Actions**

-   let merges catch up; raise background share
-   ensure final.skip_non_overlapping on
-   use argMax pattern instead of FINAL for aggregates

## IX.49.4 Lightweight deletes slow scans

**Diagnosis**

1.  strata_delete_mask_rows
1.  delete fraction per part

**Actions**

-   trigger cleanup merge (delete.mask_merge_threshold)
-   use partition drop for bulk deletes

## IX.49.5 JSON queries slow

**Diagnosis**

1.  strata_json_dynamic_paths near limit → overflow column used
1.  EXPLAIN shows overflow read

**Actions**

-   raise json.max_dynamic_paths
-   declare hot paths as typed columns

## IX.49.6 Skip index ineffective

**Diagnosis**

1.  system.index_effectiveness skip ratio
1.  index column correlation with sort key

**Actions**

-   drop index
-   choose different index type or granularity
-   add projection instead

## IX.49.7 Partial result cache low hit

**Diagnosis**

1.  strata_partial_cache_hit_ratio
1.  merge rate (new part UUIDs)

**Actions**

-   increase cache size
-   accept: heavy merging churns identities; works best on settled partitions

## IX.49.8 Vector search low recall

**Diagnosis**

1.  strata_vector_search_recall_estimate

**Actions**

-   raise ef_search
-   rebuild with larger m
-   use exact search for small filtered sets

## IX.49.9 Bulk load slower than expected

**Diagnosis**

1.  decode MB/s per core
1.  partitions per load
1.  fsync time

**Actions**

-   load by partition order
-   use native/Parquet input
-   raise parallelism

## IX.49.10 Replica lag high

**Diagnosis**

1.  strata_replication_lag_seconds
1.  network bandwidth
1.  part transfer queue

**Actions**

-   raise transfer concurrency
-   check network
-   reduce part count (merges)

# IX.50 Benchmark scenario files

Scenario definitions consumed by `strata-bench run`. One file per subsystem (VIII.26) and per reference workload (IX.35). Files are checked in under `bench/scenarios/`.

## `bench/scenarios/rt/baseline.toml`

```toml
[scenario]
name = "rt-baseline"
subsystem = "Runtime and scheduler"
profile = "HW-REF-1"
dataset = "obs"
scale_factor = 1.0
seed = 42
warmup_runs = 3
repetitions = 10
cache_state = ["cold", "warm"]
concurrency = [1, 8, 64]
load_model = "open-loop"

[durability]
mode = "fsync-group"

[metrics]
primary = "cpr"
capture_pmu = true
capture_profile = true

[gates]
max_regression_pct = 3.0
significance = 0.01
```

# IX.51 Reference Rust skeleton of the core seams

This skeleton fixes the shape of the core interfaces so that independent teams (or coding agents) build compatible pieces. It is illustrative: names may change by RFC, but the ownership, batching, and reservation rules it encodes are normative (STRATA-ARCH-03-001, -03-005, -03-007, STRATA-SYS-05-005).

```rust
// ───────────────────────── strata-types ─────────────────────────
pub type RowIdx = u32;

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Buffer { ptr: Arc<AlignedBytes>, offset: usize, len: usize }   // 64-byte aligned, tail-padded

#[derive(Clone)]
pub enum ColumnData {
    Fixed { width: u8, values: Buffer },                 // ints, floats, decimals, dates
    Bool  { bytes: Buffer },                             // 1 byte per value in memory
    Str   { offsets: Buffer, bytes: Buffer },            // offsets u32 (u64 for huge chunks)
    StrView { views: Buffer, heap: Vec<Buffer> },        // 16-byte German-string views
    Dict  { codes: Box<ColumnRef>, dict: Arc<ColumnRef> },
    List  { offsets: Buffer, child: Box<ColumnRef> },    // Array
    Struct{ children: Vec<ColumnRef> },                  // Tuple
    Map   { offsets: Buffer, keys: Box<ColumnRef>, values: Box<ColumnRef> },
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct ColumnRef { pub ty: DataType, pub data: ColumnData, pub validity: Option<Buffer>, pub null_count: u32, pub len: u32 }

pub enum Selection { All, Indices(Arc<[RowIdx]>), Bitmap(Arc<BitVec>) }

pub struct Batch { pub columns: SmallVec<[ColumnRef; 8]>, pub selection: Selection, pub rows: u32 }

// ───────────────────────── strata-memory ─────────────────────────
pub struct Reservation<'t> { tracker: &'t MemoryTracker, bytes: usize }
impl MemoryTracker {
    /// Hierarchical check leaf → root; batched via thread-local counters (±1 MiB).
    pub fn reserve(&self, bytes: usize) -> Result<Reservation<'_>, MemoryError>;
}
impl Reservation<'_> {
    pub fn grow(&mut self, extra: usize) -> Result<(), MemoryError>;
    pub fn shrink(&mut self, less: usize);
}
impl Drop for Reservation<'_> { fn drop(&mut self) { /* release */ } }

// ───────────────────────── strata-io ─────────────────────────
pub enum IoOp<'b> {
    Read  { file: FileSlot, offset: u64, buf: &'b mut AlignedBuf },
    Write { file: FileSlot, offset: u64, buf: &'b AlignedBuf },
    Fsync { file: FileSlot, data_only: bool },
}
pub struct IoToken(u64);
pub trait IoEngine {
    fn submit(&mut self, ops: &mut [IoOp<'_>], out: &mut Vec<IoToken>) -> Result<()>;
    fn reap(&mut self, f: &mut dyn FnMut(IoToken, io::Result<usize>)) -> usize;
}

// ───────────────────────── strata-runtime ─────────────────────────
pub enum WorkClass { System, Interactive, Normal, Ingest, Batch, Background }
pub enum Poll { Ready, Yield, Blocked(IoToken) }
pub trait Task: Send {
    fn class(&self) -> WorkClass;
    fn query_id(&self) -> QueryId;
    /// Run until budget exhausted at a batch boundary, I/O needed, or done.
    fn run(&mut self, budget_cycles: u64, ctx: &mut WorkerCtx) -> Poll;
}

// ───────────────────────── strata-exec ─────────────────────────
pub enum PushResult { NeedMore, Full, Finished }

pub trait Sink: Send {
    fn push(&mut self, batch: Batch, ctx: &mut ExecCtx) -> Result<PushResult>;
}

pub trait PhysicalOperator: Sink {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn initial_reservation(&self, est: &Estimates) -> MemoryRequest;
    fn finish_local(&mut self, ctx: &mut ExecCtx) -> Result<()>;
    fn finish_global(&mut self, ctx: &mut ExecCtx) -> Result<()> { Ok(()) }
    fn source(&self) -> Option<&dyn MorselSource> { None }
    fn spill(&mut self, _ctx: &mut ExecCtx, _target: usize) -> Result<usize> { Ok(0) }
    fn stats(&self) -> OperatorStats;
}

pub trait MorselSource: Send + Sync {
    /// Splits the source into morsels sized to ~1 ms of work (STRATA-SYS-11-007).
    fn morsels(&self, hint: &MorselHint) -> Vec<Morsel>;
    fn produce(&self, m: &Morsel, sink: &mut dyn Sink, ctx: &mut ExecCtx) -> Result<Poll>;
}

pub struct Pipeline { pub source: Arc<dyn MorselSource>, pub ops: Vec<Box<dyn PhysicalOperator>>, pub deps: Vec<PipelineId> }

// ───────────────────────── strata-storage ─────────────────────────
pub struct PruneContext<'a> { pub predicate: &'a Expr, pub runtime_filters: &'a [RuntimeFilter], pub columns: &'a [ColumnId] }

pub trait ScanSource: MorselSource {
    /// Partition → primary key → skip indexes; returns granule ranges per part.
    fn prune(&self, ctx: &PruneContext<'_>) -> PruneResult;
}

pub trait TableEngine: Send + Sync {
    fn insert(&self, batch: Batch, opts: &InsertOptions) -> Result<InsertAck>;
    fn scan_source(&self, snap: &Arc<CatalogSnapshot>, cols: &[ColumnId]) -> Arc<dyn ScanSource>;
    fn merge_function(&self) -> MergeFunction;   // None, Replacing, Summing, Aggregating, ...
}

// ───────────────────────── strata-index ─────────────────────────
pub enum MatchResult { None, Some, All }
pub trait IndexReader: Send + Sync {
    fn may_match(&self, granules: Range<u32>, pred: &Expr) -> MatchResult;
    fn row_ids(&self, _pred: &Expr) -> Option<RowIdSet> { None }
    fn eval_cost_ns(&self) -> u64;
}

// ───────────────────────── strata-catalog ─────────────────────────
pub struct Catalog { current: ArcSwap<CatalogSnapshot>, publisher: Mutex<Publisher> }
impl Catalog {
    #[inline] pub fn snapshot(&self) -> Arc<CatalogSnapshot> { self.current.load_full() }   // lock-free
    pub fn publish(&self, delta: CatalogDelta) -> Result<SnapshotId>;                       // single writer
}
```

-   **STRATA-ARCH-51-001 (MUST):** The skeleton's invariants — immutable `Arc` buffers, selection traveling with the batch, reservations released by `Drop`, synchronous `run` with explicit `Blocked(IoToken)`, lock-free `snapshot()` — MUST be preserved by any concrete implementation.
-   **STRATA-ARCH-51-002 (MUST):** Each trait above MUST have a conformance test suite in its crate's `tests/conformance.rs` run against every implementation including the simulation one.

# IX.52 Cross-reference: Part IX mechanisms to Part VIII requirements

| Part IX mechanism | Depends on Part VIII | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Push pipelines (IX.3) | VIII.3 runtime, VIII.11 scheduler | morsels and classes drive pipelines |
| Operator catalog (IX.20) | VIII.8 kernels, VIII.9 hash tables, VIII.14–15 sort/join | operators are compositions of kernels |
| Projections / MVs (IX.6) | VIII.7 WAL, VIII.10 part sizing, VIII.24 faults | built in flush/merge transactions |
| Indexing (IX.7) | VIII.10 granules, VIII.16 caches | indexes are per-granule metadata cached |
| Layout (IX.8) | VIII.10 codecs, VIII.31 codec matrix | layout determines compression and pruning |
| Result reuse (IX.9) | VIII.16 caches, VIII.17 snapshots | identity = snapshot / part UUID |
| Ingestion (IX.12) | VIII.6 network, VIII.7 WAL, VIII.10.3 throttling | decode → WAL → memtable |
| Distributed (IX.13) | VIII.6.5 exchange, VIII.37 | shuffle and replication |
| Concurrency (IX.4) | VIII.17 catalog, VIII.3.4 cross-thread rules | RCU and ownership |
| State machines (IX.22) | VIII.13 observability | exported state times |
| Golden plans (IX.26) | VIII.25 catalog | same queries |
| Anti-patterns (IX.28) | VIII.1.8 CPR ledger, VIII.19 harness | detection mechanisms |

# IX.53 Diagnostic queries over system tables

Two canonical diagnostic queries per system table, used by runbooks, Studio dashboards, and `strata doctor query`.

## IX.53.1 `system.query_log`

```sql
-- Top entries by user
SELECT query_id, user
FROM system.query_log
ORDER BY user DESC
LIMIT 20;
```
```sql
-- Distribution summary
SELECT count() AS entries, sum(user) AS total, max(user) AS max_value
FROM system.query_log;
```

## IX.53.2 `system.processes`

```sql
-- Top entries by user

```

## IX.53.5 `system.part_log`

```sql

```
```sql
-- Activity over the last hour, per minute
SELECT toStartOfMinute(event_time) AS m, count() AS n
FROM system.part_log
WHERE event_time >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
GROUP BY m
ORDER BY m;
```

# IX.54 Function performance targets and edge-case matrix

Initial ns/row targets on HW-REF-1 (single core, 8,192-row batches, warm). Text functions assume 24-byte strings; JSON assumes 200-byte documents. Each function's test suite MUST cover the edge cases of its family.

# IX.55 Assembly inspection list

For the 90 hottest kernel instantiations below, CI disassembles the release build (`cargo asm` / `objdump`) and asserts that the inner loop uses vector instructions of the expected width (e.g. `vpcmp*`/`ymm` for AVX2, `zmm` for AVX-512, `cmhi`/`v` registers for NEON) and contains no calls or bounds-check panics. A compiler upgrade that de-vectorizes any of them fails CI.

# IX.56 Workload capacity examples

Worked sizing for each reference workload at a representative scale using the IX.31 formulas (HW-REF-1 nodes, compression assumptions per workload).

## IX.56.1 Observability (traces/logs/metrics SaaS)

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Ingest rows/s | 2,000,000 |
| Row bytes (uncompressed) | 300 |
| Compression ratio | 10× |
| Retention days | 30 |
| **Stored TB (incl. 25% reserve)** | **194.4** |
| **Ingest cores (60% util.)** | **1.9** |
| **Merge write MB/s (WA=4)** | **120.0** |
| **Nodes (30 TB usable, 28 worker cores each), before query load** | **7** |

# IX.57 Optimization opportunity register

87 concrete optimization opportunities, each tied to one of the four levers (IX.0). Items are adopted in priority order of `expected gain × workload share ÷ (implementation cost × risk)`, and each one becomes an RFC with benchmark evidence before merging. Items marked *(evaluated)* are research spikes, not commitments.

| # | Opportunity | Lever | Expected gain | Risk | Prerequisite |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OPP-001 | Count/min/max from metadata for partially filtered queries (fully covered granules) | less work | 10–100× on counts | low | granule-level row counts and stats |
| OPP-002 | Aggregate on dictionary codes end-to-end | cheaper | 2–5× group by strings | low | per-part dictionaries; remap on merge |
| OPP-003 | Global dictionaries for LowCardinality across parts | cheaper | avoid remap; faster joins on codes | medium | dictionary service, versioning |
| OPP-004 | Sorted dictionaries enabling range predicates on codes | less work | string range filters without decode | low | order-preserving codes |
| OPP-005 | Filter on compressed FOR/BitPack data | cheaper | 1.5–3× | low | IX.21b kernels |
| OPP-006 | Late materialization with row-id lists across joins | less work | large on wide tables | medium | row-id propagation |
| OPP-007 | Top-K dynamic threshold pushed to zone maps | less work | 10–1000× for ORDER BY LIMIT | low | shared atomic threshold |
| OPP-008 | Runtime filters from aggregation HAVING | less work | moderate | medium | two-phase execution |
| OPP-009 | Bloom runtime filters sized by NDV | less work | 2–20× on star joins | low | NDV sketch on build |

# IX.58 Part IX setting presets per hardware profile

Appended to the VIII.34 preset files.

## `HW-REF-1`

```toml

[projection]
enabled = true
build_on_merge = true
max_per_table = 16

[mv]
synchronous = false
max_lag_ms_for_rewrite = 60000
parallel_transforms = 4

[json]
max_dynamic_paths = 1024
infer_types = true

[map]
bucket_count = 16
top_keys_as_columns = 32

[delete]
lightweight = true
mask_merge_threshold = 0.2

[patch_parts]
enabled = false

[final]
parallel_ranges = "auto"
skip_non_overlapping = true

[cache]
partial_results = false
partial_results_bytes = "5% RAM"

[index]
effectiveness_tracking = true
inverted.tokenizer = "unicode_words"
inverted.postings_codec = "roaring"
vector.type = "hnsw"
vector.hnsw_m = 16
vector.ef_search = 64

[ingest]
max_partitions_per_insert_block = 100
bulk_bypass_wal = true
allow_errors_ratio = 0

[exec]
compact_threshold = 0.25
pipeline_template_cache = true
adaptive_build_swap = true

[tier]
move_bytes_per_sec = "100MiB"
keep_metadata_local = true

[replication]
max_lag_ms = 1000

[distributed]
broadcast_max_bytes = "64MiB"

[advisor]
enabled = true
min_cpu_share = 0.01
```
